QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r11.claim: Only a few people in earlier communities forbade corruption, preserved religion, and obeyed their prophets.
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r11.anchor: من ينهى عن الفساد ، ويحفظ الدين

QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r12.claim: God did not destroy anyone who was reforming; those destroyed were wrongdoers.
QUSHAYRI:v2p61/r12.anchor: لم يهلك الله أحدا مصلحا وإنما هلك من كان ظالما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p214/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p214/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p214/r8.claim: ترف means luxury or a body softened by comfort; one made مترف has been made arrogant by ease, and al-Farra derives أترف from the noun for blessing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p214/r8.anchor: الترف: النعمة، صبي مترف منعم البدن، ومترف أبطرته النعمة وسعة العيش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains the implied sense as there having been no people of remaining virtue, making the exception connected despite its apparent form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r1.anchor: يراه منفيا من حيث معناه: أنه لم يكن فيهم أولو بقية، ولهذا قال الزمخشري بعد أن منع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r2.speaker: زيد بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r2.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads قليل in the nominative because the exhortation implies a negation, permitting substitution as after an explicit negative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r2.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي: إلا قليل بالرفع، لحظ أن التحضيض تضمن النفي، فأبدل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r3.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the implied meaning is they did not do so, since a question carries a shade of negation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء: المعنى فلم يكن، لأن في الاستفهام ضربا من الجحد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r4.speaker: الأخفش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash rejects treating the exception as disconnected.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r5.claim: The apparent wrongdoers are those who abandoned forbidding corruption.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r5.anchor: والظاهر أن الذين ظلموا هم تاركو النهي عن الفساد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r6.claim: Their worldly enjoyment means the love of leadership and wealth and pursuit of a comfortable life, at the expense of religious good.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r6.anchor: وما أترفوا فيه أي: ما نعموا فيه من حب الرياسة والثروة وطلب أسباب العيش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r7.claim: The next clause reports that these wrongdoers, despite abandoning the prohibition of corruption, were also criminals in other ways.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r7.anchor: واتبع استئناف إخبار عن حال هؤلاء الذين ظلموا، وإخبار عنهم أنهم مع كونهم تاركي النهي عن الفساد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī parses followed desires as coordinated with an implied clause about the few who were saved and the wrongdoers who followed desires; alternatively, it describes their punishment as a circumstance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r8.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: إن كان معناه واتبعوا الشهوات كان معطوفا على مضمر، لأن المعنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r9.claim: The pronoun in ما أترفوا فيه favors reading ما as a relative pronoun, since فيه refers back to it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r9.anchor: والظاهر أنها بمعنى الذي لعود الضمير في فيه عليها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also allows وكانوا مجرمين to coordinate with اتبعوا or to be a judgment on them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r10.anchor: وأجاز أيضا أن يكون معطوفا على اتبعوا أي: اتبعوا شهواتهم وكانوا مجرمين بذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r11.claim: Calling the final judgment an اعتراض is technically inaccurate because it closes the verse rather than interrupting two syntactically dependent parts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225/r11.anchor: ولا يسمى هذا اعتراضا في اصطلاح النحو، لأنه آخر آية، فليس بين شيئين يحتاج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225#2/r1.speaker: جعفر بن محمد والعلاء بن سيابة وأبو عمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225#2/r1.claim: They read passive وأتبعوا with a still tāʾ, understood with an omitted object as being made to follow the recompense of their luxury.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ جعفر بن محمد، والعلاء بن سيابة كذا في كتاب اللوامح، وأبو عمر في رواية الجعفي: وأتبعوا ساكنة التاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225#2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows the common active reading to mean that they followed the recompense for their luxury; the prior mention of salvation supports the sense that everyone else perished.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p225#2/r2.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى في القراءة المشهورة أنهم اتبعوا جزاء إترافهم، وهذا معنى قوي

NAHHAS:v2p306/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p306/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p306/r3.claim: لولا means why not and expresses amazement; saved few are an exception, while wrongdoers pursued luxuries.
NAHHAS:v2p306/r3.anchor: بمعنى هلا وهذا تستعمله العرب على التعجب من الشيء

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:115-116/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:115-116/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:115-116/r2.claim: Baqiyyah among earlier generations means sound judgment and reason, virtue, or restraint and self-preservation from punishment; a reading baqiyat represents the verbal noun form.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:115-116/r2.anchor: { من القرون من قبلكم أولوا بقية } من الرأي والعقل، أو أولو فضل

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:115-116/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:115-116/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:115-116/r3.claim: Only a few people whom God saved forbade corruption; the exception connects only if understood as an exception from the implied negative in the exhortation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:115-116/r3.anchor: { ينهون عن الفساد في الأرض إلا قليلا ممن أنجينا منهم } لكن قليلا منهم أنجيناهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:115-116/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:115-116/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:115-116/r4.claim: Wrongdoers pursued the pleasures and luxuries they had enjoyed; widespread oppression, following desire, abandoning the ban on wrong, and disbelief brought earlier peoples' destruction.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:115-116/r4.anchor: ما أنعموا فيه من الشهوات واهتموا بتحصيل أسبابها وأعرضوا عما وراء ذلك

BAYDAWI-FULL:11:115-116/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:115-116/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:115-116/r5.claim: Wa-ttaba'u may be coordinated with an omitted statement that they failed to forbid corruption, or be parenthetical; another reading makes it passive, meaning they were made to follow the consequences of their luxury.
BAYDAWI-FULL:11:115-116/r5.anchor: أي وأتبعوا جزاء ما أترفوا فتكون الواو للحال

DURR-FULL:v4p489/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r6.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r6.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka'b reports the Prophet taught him a reading that begins “Had there been among the generations before you.”
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r6.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب قال أقرأني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v4p489/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r7.speaker: ابن أبي مالك
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r7.claim: Ibn Abi Malik glosses “lawla” as “why then not?”
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r7.anchor: ابن أبي مالك في قوله {فلولا} قال: فهلا

DURR-FULL:v4p489/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r8.claim: Qatada says only a few people in earlier communities forbade corruption in the land.
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r8.anchor: عن قتادة في الآية قال: أي لم يكن من قبلكم من ينهى عن الفساد في الأرض إلا قليلا

DURR-FULL:v4p489/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r9.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r9.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the phrase means God saves only a small number from each people.
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r9.anchor: عن ابن جريج {إلا قليلا ممن أنجينا منهم} يستقلهم الله من كل قوم

DURR-FULL:v4p489/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r10.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r10.claim: Mujahid says wrongdoers pursued their power and luxury, acted arrogantly, and abandoned the truth.
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r10.anchor: عن مجاهد {واتبع الذين ظلموا ما أترفوا فيه} قال: في ملكهم وتجبرهم وتركهم الحق

DURR-FULL:v4p489/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses “what they were luxuriated in” as something they examined or considered.
DURR-FULL:v4p489/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس {أترفوا فيه} نظروا فيه

MUQATIL:11:115-117/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:11:115-117/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:11:115-117/r2.claim: Only a few people in earlier generations forbade corruption, meaning shirk; God saved them with the prophets while wrongdoers preferred worldly comforts.
MUQATIL:11:115-117/r2.anchor: { فلولا كان } ، يعني لم يكن { من القرون من قبلكم أولوا بقية ينهون عن الفساد } ، يعني الشرك،

QURTUBI-FULL:11:115-116/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:115-116/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:115-116/r4.claim: فلولا means why were there not among earlier nations people of virtue, obedience, religion, reason, and insight to forbid corruption, as their intelligence and God's signs required; this rebukes unbelievers.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:115-116/r4.anchor: بقية } أي أصحاب طاعة ودين وعقل وبصر. { ينهون } قومهم. { عن الفساد في الأرض

QURTUBI-FULL:11:115-116/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:115-116/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:11:115-116/r5.claim: Another reading gives لولا a negative sense: there were no such people among earlier generations, as in the verse about a town that believed.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:115-116/r5.anchor:
وقيل: لولا هاهنا للنفي أي ما كان من قبلكم كقوله:
فلولا كانت قرية آمنت

QURTUBI-FULL:11:115-116/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:115-116/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:115-116/r6.claim: The exception is disjoint: only a few of those saved from earlier peoples forbade corruption.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:115-116/r6.anchor: إلا قليلا } استثناء منقطع أي لكن قليلا. { ممن أنجينا منهم } نهوا عن الفساد في الأرض

QURTUBI-FULL:11:115-116/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:115-116/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:11:115-116/r7.claim: The few who forbade corruption are identified either as the people of Jonah or as followers of the prophets and people of truth.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:115-116/r7.anchor: قيل: هم قوم يونس لقوله: «إلا قوم يونس». وقيل: هم أتباع الأنبياء وأهل الحق

QURTUBI-FULL:11:115-116/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:11:115-116/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:11:115-116/r8.claim: Wrongdoers followed the worldly wealth and pleasures in which they luxuriated, preferring them to the afterlife, and were sinners.
QURTUBI-FULL:11:115-116/r8.anchor: واتبع الذين ظلموا } أي أشركوا وعصوا. { مآ أترفوا فيه } أي من الاشتغال بالمال واللذات

TABATABAI:11:114-116/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:114-116/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:114-116/r6.claim: The rhetorical question rebukes earlier nations for lacking a surviving group that forbade corruption; only a few people whom God rescued remained to prevent ruin.
TABATABAI:11:114-116/r6.anchor: هلا كان من القرون التي كانت من قبلكم وقد أفنيناها بالعذاب والهلاك أولوا بقية

TABRISI:11:113-116/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:113-116/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:113-116/r8.claim: Baqiyya means what remains after something is gone; describing someone as having it praises remaining virtue or goodness.
TABRISI:11:113-116/r8.anchor: والبقية ما بقي من الشيء بعد ذهابه

TABRISI:11:113-116/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:113-116/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:113-116/r9.claim: Atarafu means to become accustomed again to luxury and pleasure; a cited line calls the spoiled leaders' heads offerings, and mumtaad means one asked for help.
TABRISI:11:113-116/r9.anchor: واترفوا أي عودوا الترفه بالنعيم واللذة

TABRISI:11:115-117/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:115-117/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:115-117/r3.claim: The question means that earlier peoples had no people of discernment who forbade corruption, despite God's gifts of reason, messengers, and proofs.
TABRISI:11:115-117/r3.anchor: كان يجب أن يكون منهم قوم بهذه الصفة مع إنعام الله تعالى عليهم

TABRISI:11:115-117/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:115-117/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:115-117/r4.claim: The passage rebukes those who followed the corrupt paths of peoples such as ʿĀd and Thamūd, and marvels that they agreed in unbelief until punishment destroyed them.
TABRISI:11:115-117/r4.anchor: كيف اجتمعوا على الكفر حتى استأصلهم الله بالعذاب وأنواع العقوبات

TABRISI:11:115-117/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:115-117/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:115-117/r5.claim: The phrase 'people of discernment' is also explained as people of religion and goodness, or blessing, or discernment and obedience.
TABRISI:11:115-117/r5.anchor: قيل: أولوا بقية عناه ذوو دين وخير. وقيل: معناه ذوو بركة.

TABRISI:11:115-117/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:115-117/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:115-117/r6.claim: The few saved people who forbade corruption were the prophets and righteous believers; the exception is grammatically disconnected because the preceding construction is affirmative, not a formal negation.
TABRISI:11:115-117/r6.anchor: قليلا منهم كانوا ينهون عن الفساد وهم الأنبياء والصالحون

TABRISI:11:115-117/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:115-117/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:115-117/r7.claim: The condemned people pursued accustomed luxury and pleasures instead of the affairs of the afterlife, persisting in wrongdoing.
TABRISI:11:115-117/r7.anchor: ما عودوا من النعم والتنعم وإيثار اللذات على أمور الآخرة

TABRISI:11:115-117/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:115-117/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:115-117/r8.claim: The verse establishes the duty to forbid wrong: God censures those who neglected it and says He saved the few who did it; had the many forbidden it, they would not have perished.
TABRISI:11:115-117/r8.anchor: في الآية دلالة على وجوب النهي عن المنكر لأنه سبحانه ذمهم بترك النهي

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:114-116/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:114-116/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:114-116/r6.claim: Earlier generations had few people of religion, discernment, and virtue who forbade corruption such as polytheism, violating God's rights, and disobedience.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:114-116/r6.anchor: دين وتميز وفضل { ينهون عن الفساد في الأرض

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:114-116/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:114-116/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:114-116/r7.claim: Those few who opposed corruption and were saved were the followers of prophets and people of truth.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:114-116/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:114-116/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:11:114-116/r8.claim: Wrongdoers followed worldly luxuries and wealth, preferring pleasure and this world to the afterlife.

AKHFASH:v2p438#2/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p438#2/r5.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p438#2/r5.claim: In إلا قليل ممن أنجينا منهم, قليل is nominative as an adjective, illustrating a different exception construction.
AKHFASH:v2p438#2/r5.anchor: و {إلا قليل ممن أنجينا منهم} رفع على أن قوله {إلا قليل} صفة.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p166/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p166/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p166/r2.claim: Asim, Ibn Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisai use hamza and separated spelling for the listed forms; واتبع الذين ظلموا is joined, with an alternate Abu Amr transmission in Hud.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p166/r2.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي فأتبع سببا ثم أتبع سببا ثم أتبع سببا فأتبعه شهاب

IBNMUJAHID:v1p396/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p396/r4.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p396/r4.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, and Abū ʿAmr double tāʾ in the three follow-sabab forms; they hamzate other cited forms and double tāʾ in واتبع الذين ظلموا. Further reader groups continue next segment.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p396/r4.anchor: 31 واختلفوا فى تشديد التاء وتخفيفها من قوله ﴿ فأتبع سببا ﴾ 85

IBNMUJAHID:v1p398/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p398/r1.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p398/r1.claim: Ḥusayn al-Juʿfī reports Abū ʿAmr reading واتبع الذين ظلموا; ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī use cut forms for the other verbs and join this one alone.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p398/r1.anchor: وروى حسين الجعفى عن أبى عمرو ﴿ واتبع الذين ظلموا ﴾ رواه هرون عن حسين عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r15.claim: The verse urges commanding right and forbidding wrongdoing.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p168#2/r15.anchor: فلو لا كان من القرون من قبلكم أو لو بقية ينهون عن الفساد في الأرض ) فيه حض على الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر

SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r1.claim: لولا is exhortation carrying lament for the lost opportunity, close to the expression in 36:30.
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { فلولا كان }: " لولا " تحضيضية دخلها معنى التفجع عليهم، وهو قريب

SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r2.speaker: الخليل
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r2.claim: The report that al-Khalil said every Quranic لولا means هلا except at 37:143 is wrongly attributed: other verses use it differently, including 68:49, 48:25, and 17:74.
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r2.anchor: وما يروى عن الخليل أنه قال: " كل " لولا " في القرآن فمعناها " هلا " إلا التي في الصافات:

SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r3.claim: من القرون may attach to complete كان, meaning that people should have existed among past generations, or be an omitted circumstantial phrase for أولو بقية; من قبلكم is circumstantial to القرون.
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r3.anchor: يجوز أن يتعلق ب " كان " لأنها هنا تامة، إذ المعنى: فهلا وجد من القرون

SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r4.claim: ينهَون may be circumstantial or adjectival to أولو بقية; the adjectival analysis is preferable because the noun is specified by annexation.
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r4.anchor: و " ينهون " حال من " أولو بقية " لتخصصه بالإضافة، ويجوز أن يكون نعتا ل " أولوا بقية " وهو أولى.

SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r5.claim: An incomplete كان is weaker in meaning; on that parse من القرون must be an omitted circumstantial phrase and ينهون its accusative predicate, since most grammarians say ناقصة does not govern here.
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r5.anchor: ويضعف أن تكون " كان " هذه ناقصة لبعد المعنى من ذلك، وعلى تقديره يتعين تعلق " من القرون " بالمحذوف

SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r6.claim: The common بقية can be an intensive active adjective meaning the select or best people: one preserves the finest part of what one gives away. A Hamaasa poem witnesses بقيتكم; a proverb says men have remnants.
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r6.anchor: وقرأ العامة: " بقية " بفتح الباء وتشديد الياء، وفيها وجهان، أحدهما: أنها صفة على فعيلة للمبالغة

SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also reads بقية as the verbal noun بقوى: people who preserve themselves from God’s anger and punishment.
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r7.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " ويجوز أن تكون البقية بمعنى البقوى، كالتقية بمعنى التقوى

SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r8.speaker: فرقة
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r8.claim: A group reads بقية with light yāʾ, as the active participle of بقي, meaning a remaining group or remnant.
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r8.anchor: وقرأ فرقة/ " بقية " بتخفيف الياء وهي اسم فاعل من بقي

SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r9.speaker: أبو جعفر وشيبة
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r9.claim: Abu Jaʿfar and Shayba read بقية with ḍamma on the first consonant and sukūn on the second.
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وشيبة " بقية " بضم الفاء وسكون العين

SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r10.claim: Another reading takes بقية as a single occurrence of the verbal noun.
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r10.anchor: وقرىء " بقية " على المرة من المصدر.

SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r11.claim: في الأرض may attach to الفساد; an article-marked verbal noun governs objects, so it can certainly govern an adverb. Alternatively it is an omitted circumstantial phrase describing الفساد.
SAMIN-DURR:11:116/r11.anchor: و " في الأرض " متعلق بالفساد، والمصدر المقترن بأل يعمل في المفاعيل الصريحة

SAMIN-DURR:11:116#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#2/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#2/r1.claim: If exhortation keeps its literal force, إلا قليلا is disconnected: only a few of those saved forbade corruption, while the rest did not. A connected exception would wrongly exempt the few from exhortation; the author agrees.
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#2/r1.anchor: قال الزمشخري: " معناه: ولكن قليلا ممن أنجينا من القرون نهوا عن الفساد، وسائرهم تاركوا النهي "

SAMIN-DURR:11:116#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#2/r2.claim: A connected exception works if exhortation means negation: few generations had people of insight, with قليل accusative by the ordinary exception construction, though nominative replacement is more eloquent.
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#2/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " فإن قلت: في تحضيضهم على النهي عن الفساد معنى نفيه عنهم فكأنه قيل:

SAMIN-DURR:11:116#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#2/r3.speaker: زيد بن علي
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#2/r3.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads قليل nominative as a بدل, supporting the negation sense and more eloquent connected exception; compare 4:66.
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#2/r3.anchor: قراءة زيد بن علي " إلا قليل " بالرفع، لاحظ معنى النفي فأبدل على الأفصح

SAMIN-DURR:11:116#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#2/r4.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#2/r4.claim: Al-Farra explains the construction as فلم يكن: the exhortative question contains a shade of negation.
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#2/r4.anchor: وقال الفراء: " المعنى: فلم يكن، لأن في الاستفهام ضربا من الجحد

SAMIN-DURR:11:116#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#2/r5.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#2/r5.claim: Al-Akhfash reportedly considered the exception necessarily connected, apparently taking the clause in the negated sense.
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#2/r5.anchor: ونقل عن الأخفش أنه كان يرى تعين اتصال هذا الاستثناء، كأنه لحظ النفي.

SAMIN-DURR:11:116#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#2/r6.claim: The author takes من as partitive; al-Zamakhshari rejects that and calls it explanatory, since only those who forbade evil were saved, citing 7:165. It modifies قليلا on the first parse or clarifies it as أعني on the second.
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#2/r6.anchor: و " من " في " ممن أنجينا " للتبعيض. ومنع الزمخشري أن تكون للتبعيض، بل للبيان فقال:

SAMIN-DURR:11:116#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#3/r1.claim: If من is partitive, the phrase modifies قليلا; if explanatory, it attaches as an appositional clarification meaning أعني.
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#3/r1.anchor: فعلى الأول يتعلق بمحذوف على أنها صفة ل " قليلا " ، وعلى الثاني: يتعلق بمحذوف على سبيل البيان

SAMIN-DURR:11:116#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#3/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#3/r2.claim: The common active reading اتبع has two constructions: it can coordinate with an implied verb, or the waw can mark a circumstantial clause.
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#3/r2.anchor: العامة على " أتبع " بهمزة وصل وتاء مشددة، وباء، مفتوحتين، فعلا ماضيا مبنيا للفاعل، وفيه وجهان

SAMIN-DURR:11:116#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#3/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#3/r3.claim: If ما means their desires and blessings, the unjust followed those desires, coordinated with نهوا; if it means luxury’s consequence, the clause is circumstantial and the unjust followed their recompense.
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#3/r3.anchor: فإن قلت: علام عطف قوله: { واتبع الذين ظلموا } قلت: إن كان معناه: " واتبعوا الشهوات

SAMIN-DURR:11:116#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#3/r4.claim: ما may denote the pleasures and blessings that made them insolent, or stand for an omitted noun: the recompense for their luxury.
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#3/r4.anchor: فجوز في قوله: " ما أترفوا " وجهين أحدهما: أنه مفعول من غير حذف مضاف، و " ما " واقعة

SAMIN-DURR:11:116#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#3/r5.claim: إتراف is granting luxury or blessing; a pampered child is مترف, and الترفة can mean expansion in prosperity.
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#3/r5.anchor: والإتراف: إفعال من الترف وهو النعمة يقال: صبي مترف، أي: منعم البدن

SAMIN-DURR:11:116#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#3/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#3/r6.claim: In al-Jaʿfi’s narration, Abu Amr reads وأتبع passively, requiring an omitted noun: they were made to follow the recompense for their luxury.
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#3/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو في رواية الجعفي وجعفر " وأتبع " بضم همزة القطع وسكون التاء وكسر الباء مبنيا للمفعول

SAMIN-DURR:11:116#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#3/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#3/r7.claim: With the passive reading, ما may be relative or a verbal noun; the relative reading is more apparent because فيه refers back to it.
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#3/r7.anchor: و " ما " يجوز أن تكون بمعنى الذي، وهو الظاهر لعود الضمير في " فيه " عليه، ويجوز أن تكون مصدرية

SAMIN-DURR:11:116#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#4/r1.claim: If ما is a verbal noun, كانوا مجرمين can coordinate with أترفوا, so they followed their luxuriance and their criminality.
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#4/r1.anchor: أحدها: أن تكون عطفا على " أترفوا " إذا جعلنا " ما " مصدرية، أي: اتبعوا إترافهم وكونهم مجرمين.

SAMIN-DURR:11:116#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#4/r2.claim: Alternatively it coordinates with اتبع: they followed their desires and thereby became criminals, since desire-following is steeped in sins.
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#4/r2.anchor: والثاني: أنه عطف على " اتبع " ، أي: اتبعوا شهواتهم وكانوا مجرمين بذلك

SAMIN-DURR:11:116#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#4/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#4/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari calls the clause an intervening judgment that they were criminals; the Sheikh objects it is not a grammatical parenthesis, since it ends the verse rather than interrupting connected elements.
SAMIN-DURR:11:116#4/r3.anchor: الثالث: أن يكون اعتراضا وحكما عليهم بأنهم قوم مجرمون، ذكر ذلك الزمخشري. قال الشيخ: " ولا يسمى هذا اعتراضا

ZAJJAJ:v3p83/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p83/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p83/r1.claim: أولو بقية can mean people of discernment or obedience; in the idiom فلان في بقية, بقية means a praiseworthy merit.
ZAJJAJ:v3p83/r1.anchor: أولو تمييز، ويجوز أن يكون معناه

ZAJJAJ:v3p83/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p83/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p83/r2.claim: إلا قليلا is a disconnected exception: rather, a few of those God saved had forbidden corruption.
ZAJJAJ:v3p83/r2.anchor: استثناء منقطع، المعنى لكن قليلا ممن أنجينا منهم ممن نهى عن الفساد.

ZAJJAJ:v3p83/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p83/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p83/r3.claim: The wrongdoers followed what sustained their luxury, clung to worldly life, and rejected anything that might diminish their comfort through work or earning.
ZAJJAJ:v3p83/r3.anchor: معناه اتبعوا الشيء الذي به تدوم لهم الترفة والنعيم، وركنوا إلى الدنيا

ASAD-NOTES:11:116#n146/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:11:116#n146/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:11:116#n146/r1.claim: Asad renders the opening particle law-la as alas, referring readers to his note on 10:119.
ASAD-NOTES:11:116#n146/r1.anchor: For my rendering of the particle law-la, at the beginning of this sentence

ASAD-NOTES:11:116#n146/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:11:116#n146/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:11:116#n146/r2.claim: The passage follows the statement that God requites good-doers in 11:115 and that everyone receives their due in 11:111.
ASAD-NOTES:11:116#n146/r2.anchor: The present passage connects with the statement in the preceding verse

ASAD-NOTES:11:116#n146/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:11:116#n146/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:11:116#n146/r3.claim: Asad directs readers to his note on 6:5 for the broader implications of qarn, rendered generation.
ASAD-NOTES:11:116#n146/r3.anchor: For the wider implications of the term garn ("generation"), see surah 6, note 5.

ASAD-NOTES:11:116#n147/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:11:116#n147/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:11:116#n147/r1.claim: Tarifa means enjoying ease and plenty; mutraf describes someone enjoying or indulging in such a life.
ASAD-NOTES:11:116#n147/r1.anchor: while the participle mutraf denotes "one who enjoys a life of ease and plenty" or "indulges in the pleasures of life"

ASAD-NOTES:11:116#n147/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:11:116#n147/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:11:116#n147/r2.claim: Mutarraf adds that ease and comfort can make a person insolent or corrupt through the exclusive pursuit of pleasure, explaining Asad's rendering.
ASAD-NOTES:11:116#n147/r2.anchor: The form mutarraf has an additional significance, namely, "one whom a life of softness and ease has caused to behave insolently"

QIRAAT-ER:11:116:9#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:11:116:9#1/r1.speaker: Ḥamza
QIRAAT-ER:11:116:9#1/r1.claim: Ḥamza reads biqya with short i on bāʾ and no yāʾ gemination; it may shift from lasting quality toward an act of remaining.
QIRAAT-ER:11:116:9#1/r1.anchor: Ḥamza reading: short i-vowel on bāʾ, dropping the tashdīd on yāʾ — biqya as a lighter nominal form

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r6.claim: Lawlā is an exhortation colored by grief and regret that earlier nations failed to find guidance, like the lament “Alas for the servants.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r6.anchor: لولا هنا للتحضيض، صحبها معنى التفجع والتأسف الذي ينبغي أن يقع من البشر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r7.claim: The earlier nations in view are the people of Noah, ʿĀd, Thamūd, and those already mentioned.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r7.anchor: والقرون: قوم نوح، وعاد، وثمود، ومن تقدم ذكره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r8.claim: Baqiyya means goodness, discernment, and firmness in religion; the term came to signify the best portion a person keeps, hence the best of a people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r8.anchor: والبقية هنا يراد بها الخير والنظر والجزم في الدين، وسمي الفضل والجود بقية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r9.claim: A Hamāsa verse and the proverb about hidden stores in corners and remnants among men illustrate baqiyya for a people's finest members.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r9.anchor: وبه فسر بيت الحماسة: إن تذنبوا ثم يأتيني بقيتكم. ومنه قولهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r10.claim: The term pictures those who remain when laws and dynasties weaken from their initial strength; baqiyya is an intensive feminine active-participle form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r10.anchor: فمن ثبت في وقت الضعف فهو بقية الصدر الأول. وبقية فعيلة اسم فاعل للمبالغة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows baqiyya to mean baqwā, like taqiyya for taqwā: people who preserve themselves from God's anger and punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r11.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ويجوز أن تكون البقية بمعنى البقوى، كالتقية بمعنى التقوى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r12.speaker: فرقة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r12.claim: One group reads baqiya with a light yāʾ, as an active participle from baqiya, like shajiyat from shajiya.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r12.anchor: وقرأت فرقة: بقية بتخفيف الياء اسم فاعل من بقي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r13.speaker: أبو جعفر وشيبة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r13.claim: Abū Jaʿfar and Shayba read buqya with ḍamma on bāʾ, sukūn on qāf, and the fuʿla pattern.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r13.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر، وشيبة: بقية بضم الباء وسكون القاف، وزن فعلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r14.claim: Another reading uses the faʿla pattern from baqāhu, to watch or await; the sense is people fearful of God's retribution and alert for its arrival.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r14.anchor: وقريء: بقية على وزن فعلة للمرة من بقاه يبقيه إذا رقبه وانتظره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r15.claim: Corruption means unbelief and the sins accompanying it; the verse warns this community and urges it to forbid wrongdoing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r15.anchor: والفساد هنا الكفر وما اقترن به من المعاصي، وفي ذلك تنبيه لهذه الأمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r16.claim: The exception is disconnected: only a few of those saved forbade corruption, few relative to their communities.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r16.anchor: إلا قليلا استثناء منقطع أي: لكن قليلا ممن أنجينا منهم نهوا عن الفساد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r17.claim: A connected exception would make the exhortation mean those saved were not urged to forbid corruption, which is unsound.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r17.anchor: ولا يصح أن يكون استثناء متصلا مع بقاء التحضيض على ظاهره لفساد المعنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r18.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r18.claim: Abū Ḥayyān notes Sibawayh's treatment of a clause with exhortative lawlā as obligatory; the comparison with other grammarians is cut off in the segment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r18.anchor: والكلام عند سيبويه بالتحضيض واجب، وغيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r19.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r19.claim: The wrongdoers followed the comforts and luxuries in which they had been indulged and became criminals.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p224/r19.anchor: واتبع الذين ظلموا ما أترفوا فيه وكانوا مجرمين

ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#3/r1.claim: The opening is an exhortation carrying figurative lament: why were there not people in earlier communities to resist corruption?
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#3/r1.anchor: فلولا كان ( تحضيض فيه معنى التفجع مجازا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#3/r2.claim: Baqiyya can mean a surviving quality of judgment and reason or excellence; metaphorically it is what one selects and stores for benefit, hence one of the best people.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#3/r2.anchor: أي ذوو خصلة باقية من الرأي والعقل أو ذوو فضل

ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#3/r3.claim: Another possibility is baqiyya as baqwa, self-preservation: people protecting themselves from what brings God's anger and punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#3/r3.anchor: وجوز أن تكون البقية بمعنى البقوى كالتقية بمعنى التقوى

ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#3/r4.claim: A reading pronounces baqiyya on the measure of a single instance from baqahu, 'to wait for or watch'; it asks why people were not vigilant in fear of punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#3/r4.anchor: بزنة المرة وهو مصدر بقاه يبقيه كرماه يرميه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#3/r5.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#3/r5.claim: In a report about the delayed night prayer, Mu'adh says they waited for the Messenger of God; this usage illustrates baqina as waiting.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#3/r5.anchor: وفي الحديث عن معاذ بن جبل قال : بقينا رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#3/r6.claim: Another reading lightens the yāʾ and treats baqiya as a feminine active participle, like shajiyat.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p160#3/r6.anchor: وقريء ( بقية ) بتخفيف الياء إسم فاعل من بقي

ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر وشيبة
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r1.claim: Abū Jaʿfar and Shayba read baqiyya with ḍamma on bāʾ and sukūn on qāf.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وشيبة ( بقية ) بضم الباء وسكون القاف

ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r2.claim: The corruption among the earlier peoples is the conduct described in their stories; corruption at sea is interpreted as disbelief and its associated sins.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r2.anchor: الواقع فيما بينهم حسبما ذكر في قصصهم وفسر الفساد في البحر بالكفر وما اقترن به من المعاصي

ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r3.claim: One reading takes the exception as disconnected: rather, God saved a few because they forbade corruption.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r3.anchor: إستثناء منقطع أي ولكن قليلا منهم أنجيناهم لكونهم كانوا ينهون

ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r4.claim: Another reading says a few among those saved from the earlier nations forbade corruption, while the rest abandoned forbidding it.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r4.anchor: ولكن قليلا ممن أنجينا من القرون نهوا عن الفساد وسائرهم تاركون للنهي

ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes the first min as explanatory, since salvation belonged only to those who forbade evil, as 7:165 shows.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r5.anchor: و ( من ) الأولى بيانية لا تبعيضية لأن النجاة إنما هي للناهين وحدهم بدليل قوله سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī rejects a connected exception under the exhortative reading: it would wrongly exempt the few who already forbade corruption from the admonition.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r6.anchor: ومنع اتصال الإستثناء على ما عليه ظاهر الكلام لإستلزامه فساد المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r7.claim: If the clause is construed as negation, al-Zamakhsharī allows a connected exception: only the few saved were forbiders; raising the exception as a substitute is more eloquent.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r7.anchor: وإن اعتبر النفي كان متصلا لأنه يفيد أن القليل الناجين ناهون وأورد على ذلك القطب

ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r8.speaker: القطب
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r8.claim: Al-Quṭb objects that requests are interpreted by their meaning: “strike the people except Zayd” excludes Zayd, so a connected exception can exempt those who already forbade.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r8.anchor: أورد على ذلك القطب أن صحة السلب أو الإثبات بحسب اللفظ لازم في الخبر وأما في الطلب فيكون بحسب المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r9.speaker: صاحب الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r9.claim: Al-Kashf distinguishes the parses: making yanhawna an adjective laments that no people of virtue forbade; making it the predicate makes the connected exception incoherent.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r9.anchor: ظاهر تقرير كلام الزمخشري يشعر بأن ( ينهون ) خبر ( كان ) جعل ( من القرون ) خبرا آخر

ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r10.speaker: صاحب الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r10.claim: Al-Kashf also finds the disconnected reading defective because it implies virtuous people were not forbiders; it prefers treating “people of remnant” as a lead-in to the intended predicate, “forbiders.”
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r10.anchor: والإنقطاع على ما آثره الزمخشري أيضا يفسد لما يلزم منه أن يكون أولو بقية غير ناهين

ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r11.speaker: صاحب الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r11.claim: The wording intensifies blame: people of remaining merit should be especially expected to forbid evil, so their absence implies there were no genuinely virtuous people; the passage uses hyperbolic denial.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p161/r11.anchor: لأن ذا البقية لا يكون إلا ناهيا فإذا انتفى اللازم انتفى الملزوم وهو من باب + ولا ترى الضب بها ينجحر +

ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r1.claim: Some parse kāna as complete, ulū baqiyya as its subject, yanhawna as its adjective, min al-qurūn as an advance circumstantial phrase with partitive min, and min qablikum as a circumstantial phrase or relative adjective.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r1.anchor: أن الظاهر أن ( كان ) تامة و ( أولو بقية ) فاعلها وجملة ( ينهون ) صفته و ( من القرون ) حال متقدمة عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r2.claim: The objection is that this parse makes the exhortation and negation concern the existence of such people, whereas the issue is their forbidding; customary usage can nevertheless focus on a qualification.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r2.anchor: بل المدار على النهي تحضيضا ونفيا والتزام توجه الأمرين إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī likens the extra focus on a qualification to adding a note to a lute without producing music.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r3.anchor: والاستعمال الشائع توجه نحو ما ذكر إلى القيد كما قيل زيادة نغمة وفي الكنبور من غير طرب

ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r4.claim: The wrongdoers here are those who left the duty of forbidding corruption.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r4.anchor: واتبع الذين ظلموا ( وهم تاركو النهي عن الفساد

ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r5.claim: What they followed was the wealth, comfortable living, and worldly pleasures in which they had been indulged; tarf originally means expansion in blessing.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r5.anchor: ما أنعموا فيه من الثروة والعيش الهنيء والشهوات الدنيوية وأصل الترف التوسع في النعمة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r6.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ glosses utrifū as having returned to luxury, which is blessing.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r6.anchor: وعن الفراء معنى أترف عود الترفة وهي النعمة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r7.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r7.claim: Another explanation derives utrifū from blessings making people insolent; on this reading mā is causal or metaphorically locative.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r7.anchor: وقيل : ( أترفوا ) أي طغوا من أترفته النعم

ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r8.claim: Although the insolence explanation suits the context, al-Ālūsī says it departs from the familiar meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r8.anchor: وتعقب بأن هذا المعنى خلاف المشهور وإن صح هنا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r9.claim: Following their indulgence means devoting themselves to it and abandoning everything else.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r9.anchor: ومعنى إتباع ذلك الاهتمام به وترك غيره أي اهتموا بذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r10.speaker: بعض
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r10.claim: Some understand “criminals” as committing further crimes beyond neglecting the prohibition of corruption.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r10.anchor: أي مرتكبي جرائم غير ذلك أو كافرين متصفين بما هو أعظم الإجرام

ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r11.speaker: بعض
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r11.claim: Others take “criminals” to mean disbelievers, whose offense is graver.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r11.anchor: أو كافرين متصفين بما هو أعظم الإجرام ولكل من التفسيرين ذهب بعض

ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r12.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r12.claim: Some take the wrongdoers to include both active perpetrators of corruption and those who failed to forbid it; al-Ālūsī notes a tension with the preceding exhortation but says the issue is minor.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r12.anchor: وحمل بعضهم ( الذين ظلموا ) على ما يعم تاركي النهي عن الفساد والمباشرين له

ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r13.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r13.claim: Abū Ḥayyān treats “they were criminals” as a new sentence describing the wrongdoers: in addition to neglecting prohibition, they had other crimes.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r13.anchor: والجملة عند أبي حيان مستأنفة للأخبار عن حال هؤلاء

ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r14.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r14.claim: A precise grammarian allows the sentence to coordinate with an implied phrase, “they did not forbid.”
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162/r14.anchor: وجوز بعض المحققين أن تكون عطفا على مقدر دل عليه الكلام أي لم ينهوا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r1.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r1.claim: One proposed reconstruction is: only a few of those saved forbade corruption, and the wrongdoers followed their indulgence.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r1.anchor: وقيل : التقدير إلا قليلا ممن أنجينا منهم نهوا عن الفساد

ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r2.claim: With that reconstruction, “those who did wrong” is the expected explicit subject; under the alternative parse it includes active corrupters with negligent forbiders and implies their wrongdoing caused punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r2.anchor: وجعل الإظهار على هذا مقتضى الظاهر وعلى الأول لإدراج المباشرين مع التاركين في الحكم

ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r3.claim: The apparent al-Kashshāf parse coordinates it with nahaw as predicate, leaving the coordinated clause without a link; proposed fixes supply “their counterparts” or make nahaw an independent sentence first.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r3.anchor: وفي الكشاف ما يقتضي ظاهره بأن العطف على ( نهوا ) الواقع خير لكن فيلزم أن يكون المعطوف خبرا أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r4.claim: The usual parse coordinates “they were criminals” with “followed,” while allowing a different sense for each clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r4.anchor: وقوله تعالى : ( وكانوا مجرمين ) عطف على ( اتبع الذين ) إلخ مع المغايرة بينهما

ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r5.speaker: بعض
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r5.claim: A proposed explanatory coordination makes their criminality consist in following worldly indulgence, but al-Ālūsī considers it remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r5.anchor: وجوز أن يكون العطف تفسيرا على معنى ( وكانوا مجرمين ) بذلك الإتباع وفيه بعد

ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r6.speaker: بعض
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r6.claim: Another proposal coordinates criminality with their indulgence: pursuing desires immerses one in sins, or criminality means neglecting gratitude; al-Taqrīb objects that mā is relative because fīhi refers back to it.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r6.anchor: وأن يكون على ( أترفوا ) على معنى إتبعوا الإتراف وكونهم مجرمين لأن تابع الشهوات مغمور بالآثام

ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r7.speaker: صاحب التقريب
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r7.claim: Al-Taqrīb says mā must be relative, since the pronoun in fīhi refers to it; a source-noun reading only works if the pronoun refers back to ẓulmū.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r7.anchor: صاحب التقريب بقوله : وفيه نظر لأن ما في

ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r8.speaker: بعض
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r8.claim: The clause may instead be parenthetical, a placement rhetoricians allow at the end of speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r8.anchor: وأن تكون الجملة اعتراضا بناءا على أنه قد يكون في آخر الكلام عند أهل المعاني

ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r9.speaker: أبو جعفر والعلاء بن سيابة وأبو عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r9.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Sayyāba, and Abū ʿAmr in al-Jaʿfī’s transmission read utbiʿa with a hamza, a still tāʾ, and kasra on bāʾ, in the passive.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر والعلاء بن سيابة وأبو عمرو وفي رواية الجعفي ( وأتبع ) بضم الهمزة المقطوعة وسكون التاء

ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r10.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r10.claim: For the passive reading, an omitted noun is supplied: they were made to follow the recompense of their indulgence; mā may be source-noun or relative, with the waw circumstantial.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r10.anchor: قيل : ولا بد حينئذ من تقدير مضاف أي اتبعوا جزاء ما أترفوا و ( ما ) إما مصدرية أو موصولة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r11.claim: “They were criminals” is awkward as a condition on being saved, but can be parenthetical or a circumstantial clause explaining why the rest perished.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r11.anchor: فقد قالوا : إنه لا يحسن جعله قيدا للإنجاء إلا من حيث أنه يجري مجرى العلة لإهلاك السائر

ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r12.claim: The common active reading can also mean that God saved the few forbiders while the wrongdoers received the consequences of their indulgence and perished; the waw is circumstantial.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r12.anchor: كأنه قيل : ( أنجينا ) القليل وقد اتبع الذين ظلموا أجزاءهم فهلكوا وإذا فسرت المشهورة بذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r13.claim: On that reading, the subject of ittabaʿa may be mā itself, or the clause may use inverted word order.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p162#2/r13.anchor: فقيل : فاعل اتبع ما أترفوا أو الكلام على القلب فتدبر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206/r1.claim: Falawlā is a rebuke: why were there no people of virtue among the earlier destroyed generations to forbid corruption?
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206/r1.anchor: {فلولا} فهلا {كان من القرون} التي أهلكناهم، {من قبلكم} والآية للتوبيخ

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206/r2.claim: One explanation takes ūlū baqiyya as people with discernment.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206/r3.claim: Another explanation takes the phrase as people of obedience.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206/r4.claim: Another explanation takes the phrase as people of goodness.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206/r5.claim: The idiom dhū baqiyya describes someone who has goodness or a praiseworthy quality.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206/r5.anchor: يقال: فلان ذو بقية إذا كان فيه خير

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206#2/r1.claim: The phrase means they would undertake to prohibit corruption; its force is that there were no people of virtue among them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206#2/r1.anchor: {ينهون عن الفساد في الأرض} أي يقومون بالنهي عن الفساد، ومعناه جحد، أي: لم يكن فيهم أولو بقية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206#2/r2.claim: Illā qalīlan is a disconnected exception, meaning 'but a few'; they were followers of the prophets who forbade corruption.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206#2/r2.anchor: {إلا قليلا} هذا استثناء منقطع معناه: لكن قليلا {ممن أنجينا منهم} وهم أتباع الأنبياء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206#2/r3.claim: Atfurū means the comforts and luxuries in which the wrongdoers had been indulged; mutraf is one made prosperous and indulgent.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206#2/r3.anchor: {واتبع الذين ظلموا ما أترفوا} نعموا، {فيه} والمترف: المنعم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206#2/r4.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206#2/r4.claim: Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān glosses the phrase as what they were given.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206#2/r5.speaker: الفراء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206#2/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says it refers to the pleasures and delights to which they were habituated and their preference for worldly life over the afterlife.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p206#2/r5.anchor: وقال الفراء: [عودوا من النعيم واللذات وإيثار الدنيا]

BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r5.claim: The preceding stories show that stubborn opponents will not be persuaded by human intervention, that their worship is imitation, and that communities disputed over Moses' revealed guidance; this checks wishful hopes of accommodating them.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r5.anchor: وكان من طبع البشر البعد عن الانتهاء عن الخواطر إلا بعد التجربة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r6.claim: After the command to be patient in doing good and forbidding wrong, the verse answers the imagined objection by explaining why earlier peoples were destroyed.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r6.anchor: كان من الجائز أن يقع في فكر الاعتراض بأن يقال : ما الموجب لذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r7.speaker: الرماني
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r7.claim: Al-Rummānī allows lولا here, as in Yūnus, to express either reproach or a question.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r7.anchor: لا يجوز إطلاقه إلا فيه - قاله الرماني

BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also allows lولا as an exhortation directed to the present listener, urging people to forbid corruption.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r8.anchor: كما قال الزمخشري , ويكون للسامع لا للمهلك

BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r9.claim: The exhortation addresses listeners rather than the already destroyed: their fate strongly urges others to command right and warns them against repeating their conduct.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r9.anchor: لأن الآية لما تضمنت إهلاك المقر على الفساد كان في ذلك أقوى حث لغيرهم على الأمر والنهي

BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r10.claim: The generations meant are the previously mentioned destroyed peoples, powerful people from earlier periods.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r10.anchor: أي المهلكين الأشداء الكائنين في زمان ما

BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r11.claim: Those of baqiyya are people possessing sound judgment, goodness, and vigilance about what benefits them.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r12.claim: The root of baqiyya carries the associated ideas of gathering, strength, keeping or guarding, watching, endurance, and quality.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r12.anchor: لأن مادة ( بقي ) تدور على الجمع , ويلزمه القوة والثبات والحفظ

BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains baqiyya as the best portion a person keeps back; one described as a remnant of a people is among their finest.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r13.anchor: قال الزمخشري : لأن الرجل يستبقي مما يخرجه أجوده وافضله

BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r14.claim: They repeatedly renew their prohibition of corruption, a phrasing that signals how many corruptors there were.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r14.anchor: في كل حين إشارة غلى كثرة المفسدين

BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r15.claim: The exception denotes the few righteous people whom God saved; they were the ones who forbade corruption.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r16.claim: Min is explanatory: those saved are the same people described as the few who forbade corruption.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r16.anchor: والظاهر أن ( من ) بيانية , اي هم الذين أنجينا فإنهم نهوا عن الفساد

BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r17.claim: The wording anjaynā signals beneficial rescue that motivates opposition to corruption; using najjaynā would suggest gradual deliverance and distort the point.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r17.anchor: عبر بالإنجاء لأنه الدال على الخير الحامل للنهي عن الفساد دون التنجية الدالة على التدريج

BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r18.claim: The majority followed the path of wrongdoing, specifically by failing to forbid corruption; the unqualified wording broadens the description.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r18.anchor: أوقعوا الظلم بترك النهي عن الفساد

BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r19.claim: The passive wording focuses on the luxury bestowed on them: affluence made them arrogant and tyrannical.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r20.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r20.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r20.claim: They were entrenched criminals; their crime is a persistent severing of God's bond.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r20.anchor: أي متصفين على سبيل الرسوخ بالإجرام , وهو قطع حبل الله على الدوام

BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r21.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r21.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r21.claim: God destroyed them for their entrenched crimes; absent their criminality, destruction would count as injustice by ordinary standards.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p587#2/r21.anchor: فإن إهلاكهم على تقدير الانفكاك عن الإجرام يكون ظلما

BURSEVI:v4p128/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p128/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p128/r1.claim: Those who acted directly and those who were lax pursued corrupt advantages and indulgent pleasures.
BURSEVI:v4p128/r1.anchor: وأما المتساهلون فلما لهم في ذلك من نيل حظوهم الفاسدة

BURSEVI:v4p128/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p128/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p128/r2.claim: The clause is coordinated with following indulgence and explains destroyed nations' crime: neglecting the duty to enjoin right and forbid wrong while following desires.
BURSEVI:v4p128/r2.anchor: عطف على اتبع وهذا بيان لسبب استئصال الأمم المهلكة وهو ترك الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر واتباع الشهوات

BURSEVI:v4p128/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p128/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p128/r3.claim: A hadith says God does not punish the general populace for the elite's acts until people see wrongdoing among them and, though able to denounce it, fail to do so; then He punishes both groups.
BURSEVI:v4p128/r3.anchor: وفي الحديث : إن الله لا يعذب العامة بعمل الخاصة حتى يروا المنكر بين ظهرانيهم وهم قادرون على أن ينكروا فلا ينكرون

BURSEVI:v4p128/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p128/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p128/r4.claim: A people without truthful enjoiners and forbid­ders, who collectively persist in corruption or refuse to heed correction, are doomed.
BURSEVI:v4p128/r4.anchor: فكل قوم لم يكن فيهم آمر بالمعروف وناه عن المنكر من أرباب الصدق وهم مجتمعون على الفساد

BURSEVI:v4p128/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p128/r5.speaker: السعدي
BURSEVI:v4p128/r5.claim: Saʿdī's verses say to speak usefully against wrong if possible even when no one accepts it, and to show courage through resolve when neither hand nor tongue can act.
BURSEVI:v4p128/r5.anchor: بكو آنه دانى سخن سودمند وكر هي كس را نيايد سند

DURR-FULL:v4p490/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p490/r1.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p490/r1.claim: Qatada says wrongdoers followed worldly indulgence, which ensnared most people and distracted them from the afterlife.
DURR-FULL:v4p490/r1.anchor: عن قتادة {واتبع الذين ظلموا ما أترفوا فيه} من دنياهم وأن هذه الدنيا قد تعقدت أكثر الناس وألهتهم عن آخرتهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r1.claim: Because a corrupter seeks immediate gain, Shuayb follows his warning by pointing to God's reward for obedience, a lasting benefit better than fleeting goods.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r1.anchor: وإذ قد كانت غاية المفسد من الإفساد اجتلاب ما فيه نفع عاجل له من نوال ما يحبه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r2.claim: Baqiyya can mean permanence and imply its opposite, passing away: worldly goods vanish, while the good God calls people toward endures in this world and the next.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r2.anchor: ولفظ { بقيت } كلمة جامعة لمعان في كلام العرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r3.claim: Lawful earnings rest on natural and rightful entitlement and mutual consent, preventing resentment, hostility, and retaliation, and preserving a society's security.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r3.anchor: فأما كونه دنيويا فلأن الكسب الحلال ناشىء عن استحقاق شرعي فطري

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r4.claim: At the Farewell Pilgrimage the Prophet declared people's blood and property inviolable; Ibn Ashur likens unlawful seizure of property to bloodshed because both provoke internecine violence and loss.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r4.anchor: ومن أجل ذلك قرن الأموال بالدماء في خطبة حجة الوداع إذ قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r5.claim: Taking property without right invites attacks and plunder; obtaining it without God's approval is ingratitude that exposes it to divine punishment and loss.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r5.anchor: انتزاع الأموال بدون وجهها يفضي إلى التواثب والتثاور فتكون معرضة للابتزاز والزوال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r6.speaker: ابن عطاء الله
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r6.claim: Ibn Ata Allah says the ungrateful expose blessings to loss, while gratitude binds them securely.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r6.anchor: قال ابن عطاء الله : ( من لم يشكر النعم فقد تعرض لزوالها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r7.claim: The enduring reward is everlasting bliss, as in 19:76, where lasting good deeds bring a better reward and return with the Lord.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r7.anchor: وأما كونه أخرويا فلأن نهي الله عنها مقارن للوعد بالجزاء على تركها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r8.claim: Baqiyya may also mean virtue, good, or blessing: what is preserved is precious, as in 2:248 and in this verse's people who forbid corruption.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p139/r8.anchor: على أن لفظ ( البقية ) يحتمل معنى آخر من الفضل في كلام العرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r1.claim: Al-qurun means nations or communities; Ibn ʿAshūr refers to his discussion at the beginning of al-Anʿam.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r1.anchor: والقرون : الأمم . وتقدم في أول الأنعام .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r2.claim: Baqiyya means virtue and goodness; calling virtue a ‘remainder’ became a conventional metaphor because people do not discard what is precious.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r2.anchor: والبقية : الفضل والخير . وأطلق على الفضل البقية كناية غلبت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r3.speaker: رويَشد بن كثير الطائي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r3.claim: The poet’s use of بقيتكم (‘your remainder’) illustrates the term for a community’s eminent, virtuous people; a proverb similarly speaks of ‘remnants’ among men.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r3.anchor: قال رويشد بن كثير الطائي : إن تذنبوا ثم تأتيني بقيتكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r4.claim: The people meant are followers of messengers who possess virtue, piety, and knowledge of the revealed law, not the messengers themselves; they warn their communities against corruption.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r4.anchor: والمعنى هنا : أولو فضل ودين وعلم بالشريعة ، فليس المراد الرسل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r5.claim: Corruption includes sins and disrupted social conditions. Prohibition restrains reckless sin and repairs conditions, averting the decline that befell the Israelites when no one admonished them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r5.anchor: والفساد : المعاصي واختلاف الأحوال ، فنهيهم يردعهم عن الاستهتار في المعاصي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r6.claim: The verse praises the Prophet’s Companions: some called Quraysh to faith until they believed; among other peoples they called people to faith and uprightness and taught religion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r6.anchor: وفي هذا تنويه بأصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فإنهم أولو بقية من قريش

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r7.claim: The wording ‘before you’ hints at the glad tiding that Muslims will not be like those prior communities.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r7.anchor: وفي قوله : { من القرون من قبلكم } إشارة إلى البشارة بأن المسلمين لا يكونون كذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r8.speaker: ابن جماز عن أبي جعفر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r8.claim: Ibn Jammāz from Abū Jaʿfar reads biqya with kasra on bāʾ, a still qāf, and a light yāʾ; Ibn ʿAshūr calls it a dialect form absent from lexicons, perhaps suggesting dignified bearing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن جماز عن أبي جعفر ( بقية ) بكسر الباء الموحدة وسكون القاف وتخفيف التحتية فهي لغة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r9.claim: ‘Except a few’ is a detached exception from ‘people of virtue,’ and by implication from the former nations; its accusative marks disconnection, while a connected exception would be nominative by substitution.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r9.anchor: و { إلا قليلا } استثناء منقطع من { أولوا بقية } وهو يستتبع الاستثناء من القرون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r10.claim: The detached exception corrects a possible implication that every pre-Muslim nation lacked people of virtue: a few did have them, while the verse censures the many who lacked them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p183/r10.anchor: ولكن لما كان معنى التحضيض قد يوهم أن جميع القرون التي كانت قبل المسلمين قد عدموا أولي بقية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r1.claim: Min is explanatory, clarifying that the few whom God saved from those nations were the people who forbade corruption, followers of the messengers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r1.anchor: و ( من ) في قوله : { ممن أنجينا } بيانية ، بيان للقليل لأن الذين أنجاهم الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r2.claim: Their admonition led to salvation as the cause of repentance: they stopped sinning and were thereby saved from the Fire, which no one can repel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r2.anchor: وفي البيان إشارة إلى أن نهيهم عن الفساد هو سبب إنجاء تلك القرون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r3.claim: The wording omits an idea to be supplied: they repented and abandoned corruption on earth, so they escaped the Fire.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r3.anchor: ودل قوله : { ممن أنجينا منهم } على أن في الكلام إيجاز حذفف تقديره : فكانوا يتوبون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r4.claim: The clause makes explicit the implication of the exception: most neither forbade corruption nor desisted, and followed their indulgence, much as 2:34 spells out the implication of its exception.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r4.anchor: وجملة { واتبع الذين ظلموا } معطوفة على ما أفاده الاستثناء من وجود قليل ينهون عن الفساد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r5.claim: The passage admonishes sinful Muslims too, since they are never entirely free of wronging themselves.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r5.anchor: وفي الآية عبرة وموعظة للعصاة من المسلمين لأنهم لا يخلون من ظلم أنفسهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r6.claim: Following what they were indulged in means devoting themselves to it and pursuing it as a follower pursues the one followed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r6.anchor: واتباع ما أترفوا فيه هو الانقطاع له والإقبال عليه إقبال المتبع على متبوعه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r7.claim: They were granted luxury, abundance, and ease by God, but failed to thank Him for it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r7.anchor: وأترفوا : أعطوا الترف ، وهو السعة والنعيم الذي سهله الله لهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r8.claim: They were criminals in their pursuit of luxury because they were ungrateful; enjoying luxury with gratitude would not be exclusive devotion to it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r8.anchor: و { كانوا مجرمين } أي في اتباع الترف فلم يكونوا شاكرين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r9.claim: A further ellipsis supplies that the fate of criminals became due upon them, preparing for the next verse’s statement that God would not destroy towns unjustly.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p185/r9.anchor: وفي الكلام إيجاز حذف آخر ، والتقدير : فحق عليهم هلاك المجرمين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r1.claim: Lawlā normally urges action, but here it conveys grief and regret over earlier nations that failed to find guidance, as in “Alas for the servants.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r1.anchor: لولا هي التي للتحضيض- لكن يقترن بها هنا معنى التفجع والتأسف الذي ينبغي أن يقع من البشر على هذه الأمم التي لم تهتد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r2.claim: The earlier generations include Noah’s people, ʿĀd, Thamūd, and those previously mentioned.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r2.anchor: والقرون من قبلكم هم قوم نوح وعاد وثمود ومن تقدم ذكره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r3.claim: A qarn is a people joined in one long period; after reporting estimates of 100, 80, or 30 years, Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers 100 years, corroborated by a Prophetic report.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r3.anchor: والقرن من الناس: المقترنون في زمان طويل أكثره- فيما حد الناس- مائة سنة، وقيل ثمانون وقيل غير ذلك إلى ثلاثين سنة والأول أرجح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r4.claim: A Prophetic report says that within 100 years none of those alive on earth that night would remain; Ibn ʿUmar explains that it marks the end of that generation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r4.anchor: لقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أرأيتكم ليلتكم هذه فإن إلى رأس مائة سنة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r5.claim: Baqiyya means discernment, reason, resolve, and firmness in religion; as institutions weaken from their beginnings, the steadfast are the remnant of the first generation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r5.anchor: وبقية هنا يراد بها النظر والعقل والحزم والثبوت في الدين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r6.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r6.claim: One group reads baqiyya with a light yāʾ, treating faʿīla as faʿla.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r6.anchor: وقرأت فرقة: «بقية» بتخفيف الياء وهو رد فعيلة إلى فعلة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر وشيبة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r7.claim: Abū Jaʿfar and Shayba read it with ḍamma on the bāʾ and a still qāf, on the faʿla pattern.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وشيبة «بقية» بضم الباء وسكون القاف على وزن فعلة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r8.claim: Corruption on earth means unbelief and the sins accompanying it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r8.anchor: والفساد في الأرض هو الكفر وما اقترن به من المعاصي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r9.claim: The verse warns Muḥammad’s community and urges it to change wrongdoing and forbid corruption.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r9.anchor: وهذه الآية فيها تنبيه لأمة محمد وحض على تغيير المنكر والنهي عن الفساد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r10.claim: The exception denotes the few people saved with their prophets, few compared with their communities.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r10.anchor: ثم استثنى الله تعالى القوم الذين نجاهم مع أنبيائهم وهم قليل بالإضافة إلى جماعاتهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r11.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r11.claim: Sibawayh treats qalīlan as an accusative disconnected exception because the wording is affirmative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r11.anchor: وقليلا نصب على الاستثناء وهو منقطع عند سيبويه، والكلام عنده موجب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r12.speaker: غيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r12.claim: Other grammarians regard the statement as semantically negative: there were no people of discernment among them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r12.anchor: وغيره يراه منفيا من حيث معناه أنه لم يكن فيهم أولو بقية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r13.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r13.claim: Most readers use the active form of ittabaʿa.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r13.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «واتبع» على بناء الفعل للفاعل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r14.speaker: حفص بن محمد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r14.claim: Ḥafṣ ibn Muḥammad reads ittubiʿa in the passive; the reading is also reported from Abū ʿAmr.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r14.anchor: وقرأ حفص بن محمد: «واتبع» على بنائه للمفعول، ورويت عن أبي عمرو

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r15.claim: They followed the consequence of the luxuries they had enjoyed; the pampered person is diverted from truth by luxury until he perishes.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r15.anchor: وما أترفوا فيه أي عاقبة ما نعموا به- على بناء الفعل للمفعول- والمترف: المنعم الذي شغلته ترفته عن الحق حتى هلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r16.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r16.claim: Ibn ʿUmar explains the Prophetic 100-year report as saying that the generation would be cut off.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214/r16.anchor: قال ابن عمر: يريد أنها تخرم ذلك القرن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214#2/r1.claim: The poetic word al-mumtād means the person asked for something; māda-hu means “he asked him.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p214#2/r1.anchor: يريد المسئول، يقال ماده: إذا سأله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p170#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p170#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p170#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Farrāʾ explain فلولا كان as فلم يكن, meaning there were not such people.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p170#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس والفراء المعنى فلم يكن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p170#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p170#2/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p170#2/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba interprets فلولا as an urging question: why were there not such people among earlier generations?
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p170#2/r2.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة المعنى فهلا كان من القرون من قبلكم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p170#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p170#2/r3.speaker: ابن جماز عن أبي جعفر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p170#2/r3.claim: Ibn Jammaz reports from Abū Jaʿfar a reading with kasra on bāʾ, still qāf, and ungeminated yāʾ in بقية.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p170#2/r3.anchor: وروى ابن جماز عن أبي جعفر أولو بقية بكسر الباء وسكون القاف وتخفيف الياء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p170#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p170#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p170#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains أولو بقية as people of religion; Ibn Qutayba says the expression describes a people with firmness and virtue.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p170#2/r4.anchor: أحدها أولو دين قاله ابن عباس قال ابن قتيبة يقال قوم لهم بقية وفيهم بقية إذا كانت بهم مسكة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p170#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p170#2/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p170#2/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj reports two further senses, discernment and obedience, and says having a remainder means possessing excellence.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p170#2/r5.anchor: والثاني أولو تمييز والثالث أولو طاعة ذكرهما الزجاج وقال إذا قلت فلان فيه بقية فمعناه فيه فضل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p170#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p170#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p170#2/r6.claim: إلا قليلا is a disconnected exception: rather, only a few of those God saved forbade corruption.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p170#2/r6.anchor: استثناء منقطع أي لكن قليلا ممن أنجينا منهم ممن نهى عن الفساد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p170#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p170#2/r7.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p170#2/r7.claim: Muqātil says earlier communities had no people forbidding sins and idolatry except a few whom God saved from punishment alongside the messengers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p170#2/r7.anchor: قال مقاتل لم يكن من القرون من ينهى عن المعاصي والشرك إلى قليلا ممن أنجينا من العذاب مع الرسل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p360#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p360#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p360#2/r1.claim: Earlier peoples should have had righteous remnants who restrained the evils, abominations, and corruption occurring among them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p360#2/r1.anchor: بقايا من أهل الخير، ينهون عما كان يقع بينهم من الشرور والمنكرات والفساد في الأرض

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p360#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p360#2/r2.speaker: author
