IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p360#2/r2.claim: Only a small number of such people existed; God saved them when punishment suddenly descended.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p360#2/r2.anchor: قد وجد منهم من هذا الضرب قليل، لم يكونوا كثيرا، وهم الذين أنجاهم الله عند حلول غيره، وفجأة نقمه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p360#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p360#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p360#2/r3.claim: God commanded this distinguished Muslim community to enjoin right and forbid wrong, as in 3:104.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p360#2/r3.anchor: أمر تعالى هذه الأمة الشريفة أن يكون فيها من يأمر بالمعروف وينهى عن المنكر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p360#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p360#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p360#2/r4.claim: A prophetic report warns that when people see wrongdoing and fail to change it, God may soon make punishment encompass them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p360#2/r4.anchor: إن الناس إذا رأوا المنكر فلم يغيروه، أوشك أن يعمهم الله بعقاب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p361/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p361/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p361/r1.claim: The wrongdoers persisted in their sins and evils, disregarded those who objected, and were overtaken by punishment as criminals.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p361/r1.anchor: استمروا على ما هم فيه من المعاصي والمنكرات، ولم يلتفتوا إلى إنكار أولئك، حتى فجأهم العذاب

JISHUMI:v5p3581/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r1.claim: Baqiyya is what remains after something is gone; it is the noun of preserving, and having baqiyya means doing something praiseworthy.
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r1.anchor: البقية: ما بقي من الشيء بعد ذهابه، وهو الاسم من الإبقاء، ويقال: في فلان بقية

JISHUMI:v5p3581/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r2.speaker: القتبي
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r2.claim: Al-Qutaybi glosses baqiyya as goodness remaining in a person.
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r2.anchor: وقال [القتبي]: قولهم: بقية؛ أي: مسكة فيهم من خير

JISHUMI:v5p3581/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r3.claim: Preserving one's self and guarding it mean protecting oneself from harms.
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r3.anchor: استبقى النفس وتوقه أي: تحرز من الآفات

JISHUMI:v5p3581/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r4.speaker: ابن عرفة
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r4.claim: Taraf is luxury; Ibn ʿArafa says the mutraf is left free to do as he wishes, hence the term for unrestrained enjoyment.
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عرفة: المترف المتروك يصنع ما يشاء، لا يمنع منه

JISHUMI:v5p3581/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r6.claim: Lawla means 'why did they not' and expresses amazement or rebuke; it can also be a reproach particle.
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r6.anchor: (لولا): معناه: هلا، ولم لا، وهو تعجيب وتوبيخ

JISHUMI:v5p3581/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r7.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r7.claim: Another analysis takes لو as a wish particle joined to لا, as هل is joined to لا in censure.
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r7.anchor: (لو) حرف للتمني، وصل بها (لا)، كما وصل ب (هل)، عند التبكيت

JISHUMI:v5p3581/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r8.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r8.claim: Abu Muslim takes ينهون as the answer to lawla.
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r8.anchor: وجواب (لولا) قوله: ينهون، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v5p3581/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r10.claim: Qalilan is accusative as an exception.

JISHUMI:v5p3581/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r11.claim: After mentioning destroyed nations, the commentary says widespread disbelief caused their ruin; a believing remnant would have been spared by mercy.
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r11.anchor: لما تقدم ذكر إهلاك الأمم ببن تعالى أنهم أتوا من جهتهم، ولو كان فيهم مؤمنون لما استأصلناهم

JISHUMI:v5p3581/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r12.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r12.claim: The phrase can mean people retaining religion and reason, or people of goodness and obedience, who forbid indecency and prevent a general punishment.
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r12.anchor: ذووا بقية من دين وعقل، وقيل: أولو خير وطاعة

JISHUMI:v5p3581/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r13.speaker: الأصم وأبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r13.claim: Al-Asamm and Abu Muslim say they are people who fear punishment for themselves and guard themselves from Hell.
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r13.anchor: من كان يتقي على نفسه من عذاب، أي: يرحم نفسه فلا يعرضها لعذاب النار، عن الأصم، وأبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v5p3581/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r14.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r14.claim: Abu ʿAli reads it as a remnant of the elders and asks why any did not remain despite the many messengers and proofs, forbidding corruption.
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r14.anchor: فكيف اجتمعوا على الكفر فعمهم العذاب، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v5p3581/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r15.claim: The few saved are a disconnected exception: followers of the prophets and people of truth who enjoined right and escaped destruction.
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r15.anchor: لكن قليلا منهم أمروا بالمعروف ونهوا عن المنكر وهم أتباع الأنبياء، وأهل الحق

JISHUMI:v5p3581/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r16.speaker: ابن جريج
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r16.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the people of goodness were few in every community.
JISHUMI:v5p3581/r16.anchor: قال ابن جريج: استقل أهل الخير من كل قوم

JISHUMI:v5p3582/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3582/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3582/r1.claim: The wrongdoers harmed themselves with sins and followed worldly adornment and pleasures, forgetting the Benefactor and gratitude.
JISHUMI:v5p3582/r1.anchor: ثم عاد الكلام إلى الأكثر فقال: (واتبع الذين ظلموا) أنفسهم بالمعاصي

JISHUMI:v5p3582/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3582/r2.speaker: الفراء
JISHUMI:v5p3582/r2.claim: Al-Farraʾ says they followed the luxuries, pleasures, and worldly means to which they had grown accustomed.
JISHUMI:v5p3582/r2.anchor: اتبعوا ما عودوا من النعيم واللذات وأسباب الدنيا، عن الفراء

JISHUMI:v5p3582/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3582/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v5p3582/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses the phrase as enjoying luxury.

JISHUMI:v5p3582/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3582/r4.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v5p3582/r4.claim: Mujahid says they acted tyrannically in their kingship.

JISHUMI:v5p3582/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3582/r5.speaker: author والأصم
JISHUMI:v5p3582/r5.claim: The author explains that they persisted in wrongdoing; al-Asamm alternatively says they were polytheists.
JISHUMI:v5p3582/r5.anchor: وكانوا مجرمين) أي: مصرين على الجرم، وقيل: مشركين، عن الأصم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p411#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p411#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p411#3/r1.claim: Here ‘lawlā’ means ‘why was there not?’ or ‘would that there had been?’—that is, ‘halā.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p411#3/r1.anchor: فلولا كان من القرون } فهلا كان وقد حكوا عن الخليل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p411#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p411#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p411#3/r2.claim: The author doubts the report that al-Khalīl said every Qur’anic ‘lawlā’ means ‘halā’ except in al-Ṣāffāt, since examples outside it mean ‘if not for,’ including 68:49, 48:25, and 17:74.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p411#3/r2.anchor: وما صحت هذه الحكاية ففي غير الصافات { لولا أن تداركه نعمة من ربه لنبذ بالعراء }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p411#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p411#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p411#3/r3.claim: ‘People of baqiyya’ means people of merit and goodness; the term denotes quality because people preserve the best of what they give away.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p411#3/r3.anchor: أولو فضل وخير . وسمى الفضل والجودة بقية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p411#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p411#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p411#3/r4.claim: A line in the Ḥamāsa uses ‘baqiyyatukum’ for the best remnant of a people, witnessing the sense ‘the best.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p411#3/r4.anchor: وبه فسر بيت الحماسة : إن تذنبوا ثم يأتيني بقيتكم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p411#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p411#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p411#3/r5.claim: The proverb ‘in corners are hidden things, and among men are remnants’ likewise uses ‘remnants’ for the best people.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p411#3/r5.anchor: ومنه قولهم : في الزوايا خبايا ، وفي الرجال بقايا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p411#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p411#3/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p411#3/r6.claim: Alternatively, ‘baqiyya’ may mean ‘baqwā,’ describing people who persevere in self-restraint and protect themselves from God’s anger and punishment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p411#3/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون البقية بمعنى البقوى ، كالتقية بمعنى التقوى ، أي : فهلا كان منهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p411#3/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p411#3/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p411#3/r7.claim: A reading has ‘ūlū baqiya’ on the pattern of ‘luqya,’ from ‘baqāhu yubqīhi,’ meaning to watch, observe, or await him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p411#3/r7.anchor: من بقاه يبقيه إذا راقبه وانتظره ومنه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r1.claim: People of discernment are watchful of God and afraid of His vengeance, as though they await it with apprehension.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r1.anchor: فلو كان منهم أولو مراقبة وخشية من انتقام الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r2.claim: He takes the exception as disconnected: only a few of those rescued forbade corruption; the rest left it unopposed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r2.anchor: معناه : ولكن قليلا ممن أنجينا من القرون نهوا عن الفساد ،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r3.claim: Min is explanatory, not partitive, since the saved were precisely those who forbade evil, as 7:165 confirms.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r3.anchor: حقها أن تكون للبيان لا للتبعيض ؛ لأن النجاة إنما هي للناهين وحدهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r4.claim: A connected exception under the surface reading gives the false sense that all but a few people of discernment were urged to forbid corruption.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r4.anchor: كان المعنى فاسدا ؛ لأنه يكون تخصيصا لأولى البقية على النهي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r5.claim: If the exhortation implies that people did not forbid corruption, the exception can be connected; accusative is valid, though nominative as a substitute is more eloquent.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r5.anchor: كان استثناء متصلا ومعنى صحيحا ، وكان انتصابه على أصل الاستثناء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r6.claim: The wrongdoers are those who abandoned enjoining right and forbidding wrong, a central religious duty, and pursued luxury, status, wealth, and ease.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r6.anchor: أراد بالذين ظلموا : تاركي النهي عن المنكرات ، أي : لم يهتموا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r7.claim: In al-Jaʿfi's transmission, Abu ʿAmr reads the phrase as the wrongdoers being made to follow the recompense of their indulgence.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو في رواية الجعفي ، ( واتبع الذين ظلموا ) ، يعني : واتبعوا جزاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r8.claim: On the familiar reading, the phrase may mean that they followed the recompense of their luxury; this fits the preceding mention of rescue and the others' destruction.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r8.anchor: في القراءة المشهورة : أنهم اتبعوا جزاء إترافهم . وهذا معنى قوي لتقدم الإنجاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r9.claim: If the phrase means they pursued their appetites, its conjunction is with the implied clause that the few forbade corruption.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r9.anchor: إن كان معناه : واتبعوا الشهوات ، كان معطوفا على مضمر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r10.claim: If it means they followed their recompense, the waw is circumstantial: the few were saved while the wrongdoers followed their penalty.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r10.anchor: وإن كان معناه واتبعوا جزاء الإتراف ، فالواو للحال ، كأنه قيل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r11.claim: The criminal description can attach to their indulgence; their crime may also mean neglecting gratitude.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r11.anchor: على أترفوا أي : اتبعوا الإتراف وكونهم مجرمين ؛ لأن تابع الشهوات

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r12.claim: Alternatively, the description attaches to their following their appetites, or is a parenthetical judgment that they were criminals.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p412/r12.anchor: أو على اتبعوا ، أي اتبعوا شهواتهم وكانوا مجرمين بذلك . ويجوز أن يكون اعتراضا

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p510/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p510/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p510/r1.claim: The phrase can describe people of obedience, discernment, or fear of God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p510/r1.anchor: أولو بقية } فيه ثلاثة أوجه : أحدها : أولو طاعة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p510/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p510/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p510/r2.claim: One view says wrongdoers pursued the continuing blessings in which they lived, as a gradual enticement toward ruin.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p510/r2.anchor: اتبعوا على ظلمهم ما أترفوا فيه من استدامة نعمهم استدراجا لهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p510/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p510/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p510/r3.claim: A second view says they were seized for their wrongdoing amid the luxuries they enjoyed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p510/r3.anchor: أخذوا بظلمهم فيما أترفوا فيه من نعمهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p510/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p510/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p510/r4.claim: Mutraf refers to a person living in ease and luxury.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p510/r4.anchor: فيما أترفوا فيه من نعمهم . والمترف : المنعم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p510/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p510/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p510/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses the phrase as 'look into it.'

MUJAHID:v1p309/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p309/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p309/r1.claim: The wrongdoers followed their kingship and arrogance, abandoning the truth.
MUJAHID:v1p309/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ واتبع الذين ظلموا ما أترفوا فيه ﴾ يعني في ملكهم وتجبرهم وتركهم الحق

NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r1.claim: Lawlā here is an exhortation or rebuke and is used specifically with a verb.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r1.anchor: فهلا كان هو موضوع للتحضيض ومخصوص بالفعل

NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r2.claim: Ūlū baqiyya means people of virtue and goodness; the name comes from a person keeping the best of what he gives away, and the proverb calls the best remnants.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r2.anchor: أولو فضل وخير وسمى الفضل والجودة بقية لأن الرجل يستبقى مما يخرجه اجوده وأفضله

NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r3.claim: Muḥammad and his community should wonder that among the nations destroyed in this sūra there were so few people of reason and religion who forbade disbelief and sins.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r3.anchor: عجب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وأمته إن لم يكن فى الأمم التى ذكر الله اهلاكهم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r4.claim: The exception is disconnected: rather, a few of those saved forbade corruption, while the rest left the prohibition undone.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r4.anchor: استثناء منقطع أى ولكن قليلا ممن انجينا من القرون نهوا عن الفساد وسائرهم تاركون لللنهى

NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r5.claim: Min is explanatory, not partitive, since only those who forbade evil were saved, as stated in 7:165.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r5.anchor: ومن فى ممن انجينا للبيان لا للتبعيض لأن النجاة للناهين وحدهم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r6.claim: Those who wronged are the people who abandoned forbidding evil; the clause coordinates with the implied account that a few forbade it, and they followed their desires.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r6.anchor: أى التاركون للنهى عن المنكر وهو عطف على ممضمر أى إلا قليلا ممن انجينا منهم نهوا عن الفساد

NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r7.claim: They pursued luxury: love of leadership and wealth and the means to an easy life, abandoning the command to enjoin good and forbid evil.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r7.anchor: من حب الرياسة والثروة وطلب أسباب العيش الهنيء ورفضوا الأمر بالمعروف والنهى عن المنكر

NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r8.claim: The final phrase is parenthetical and judges them to be criminals.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p175#3/r8.anchor: ﴿ وكانوا مجرمين ﴾ اعتراض وحكم عليهم بأنهم قوم مجرمون

RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r1.claim: After explaining the destruction of earlier peoples, Razi gives the absence of people who forbade corruption as its first cause.
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r1.anchor: اعلم أنه تعالى لما بين أن الأمم المتقدمين حل بهم عذاب الاستئصال بين أن السبب فيه أمران

RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r2.speaker: الخليل
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r2.claim: Al-Khalil is reported to say that lولا means 'why not' (هلا) everywhere in the Qur'an except in al-Saffat.
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r2.anchor: وحكي عن الخليل أنه قال كل ما كان في القرآن من كلمة لولا فمعناه هلا إلا التي في الصافات

RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r3.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r3.claim: The author of al-Kashshaf rejects that attribution, citing Qur'anic lولا clauses outside al-Saffat at 68:49, 48:25, and 17:74.
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r3.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : وما صحت هذه الرواية عنه بدليل قوله تعالى في غير الصافات

RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r4.claim: Ūlū baqiyya means people of virtue and goodness: the best of what a person gives is what he keeps back, hence the idiom for the best people and the proverb about hidden treasures and human remnants.
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r4.anchor: وقوله : { أولوا بقية } فالمعنى أولو فضل وخير

RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r5.claim: Another explanation takes baqiyya as baqwā, like taqiyya for taqwā: people who persist in guarding themselves from God's displeasure.
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون البقية بمعنى البقوى كالتقية بمعنى التقوى أي فهلا كان منهم ذو بقاء

RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r6.claim: A variant reads ūlū baqiyya on the pattern of laqiya, from a verb meaning to watch or await; it describes people watchful and fearful of God's vengeance.
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r6.anchor: وقرىء { أولوا بقية } بوزن لقية من بقاه يبقيه إذا راقبه وانتظره

RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r7.claim: The exception cannot be connected to the call for people of virtue to forbid corruption, which would absurdly exempt the few saved from that encouragement; it is disconnected: only a few of the saved forbade it.
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r7.anchor: ثم قال : { إلا قليلا } ولا يمكن جعله استثناء متصلا لأنه على هذا التقدير يكون ذلك ترغيبا

RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r8.claim: The second cause of exterminating punishment was that wrongdoers followed what they luxuriated in, neglecting the central religious duty to command right and forbid wrong while pursuing desires, pleasures, and status.
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r8.anchor: والسبب الثاني : لنزول عذاب الاستئصال قوله : { واتبع الذين ظلموا ما أترفوا فيه }

RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r9.claim: Taraf is luxury; a well-nourished child is called mutraf, and a mutraf is someone whom comfort and abundant living have made insolent.
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r9.anchor: والترفه النعمة وصبي مترف إذا كان منعم البدن ، والمترف الذي أبطرته النعمة وسعة المعيشة

RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r10.speaker: أبو عمرو في رواية الجعفي
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r10.claim: Abu Amr, in al-Jaʿfi's transmission, reads ittabaʿa; the sense is that the wrongdoers followed unlawful things in which they had been indulged.
RAZI-FULL:v18p60/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو في رواية الجعفي { واتبع الذين ظلموا ما أترفوا } أي واتبعوا حراما أترفوا فيه

RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r1.speaker: مثبتو الجن والشياطين
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r1.claim: Proponents of immaterial jinn describe celestial spirits as stronger causes of human spirits, guiding their human counterparts through dreams or waking inspiration.
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r1.anchor: تلك الأرواح الفلكية تعين أولادها على مصالحها

RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r2.speaker: مثبتو الجن والشياطين
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r2.claim: They say a human soul strongly connected to its celestial source can display extraordinary and supernatural acts.
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r2.anchor: ظهرت عليه أفعال عجيبة وأعمال خارقة للعادات فهذا تفصيل مذاهب من يثبت الجن والشياطين

RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r3.speaker: قوم من الفلاسفة
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r3.claim: Some philosophers object that immaterial beings cannot perceive particulars or cause particular actions.
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r3.anchor: أن قوما من الفلاسفة طعنوا في هذا المذهب وزعموا أن المجرد يمتنع عليه إدراك الجزئيات

RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī replies that the soul judging a particular person to be human rather than a horse must perceive particulars as well as universals.
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r4.anchor: يمكننا أن نحكم على هذا الشخص المعين بأنه إنسان وليس بفرس

RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r5.claim: Even if an immaterial soul cannot initially perceive particulars, it may do so through bodily instruments, which jinn could have in the ether or frigid spheres.
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r5.anchor: يمكنها أن تدرك الجزئيات بواسطة الآلات الجسمانية

RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r6.claim: Al-Rāzī argues that different kinds of bodies may share volume and magnitude yet have different natures; a subtle kind could be alive, intelligent, powerful, and self-shaping.
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r6.anchor: الأجسام متساوية في الحجمية والمقدار وهذان المعنيان أعراض

RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r7.claim: He argues that subtle bodies need not be torn by wind, comparing their possible penetration to lightning fire passing through stone and iron.
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r7.anchor: لم لا يجوز أن يقال : أحد أنواع الأجسام أجسام لطيفة نفاذة

RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r8.claim: On this possibility, jinn could penetrate and affect human bodies and remain active until their appointed term; no proof rules out these possibilities.
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r8.anchor: فكل هذه الأحوال احتمالات ظاهرة والدليل لم يقم على إبطالها

RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r9.claim: Against the social-contact objection, al-Rāzī says friendship or enmity need not occur with everyone, and individuals do not know one another's experiences, so the matter remains possible.
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r9.anchor: لا يجب حصول تلك الصداقة والعداوة مع كل واحد وكل واحد لا يعرف إلا حال نفسه

RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r10.claim: Al-Rāzī denies that belief in jinn and angels necessarily impugns the prophets' mission, deferring the fuller answer.
RAZI-FULL:v1p72#2/r10.anchor: لا نسلم أن القول بوجود الجن والملائكة يوجب الطعن في نبوة الأنبياء

STUDYQURAN:11:116/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:116/r1.speaker: al-Ṭūsī
STUDYQURAN:11:116/r1.claim: Al-Ṭūsī says the question is meant to produce wonder that past communities had only a few righteous people, while the rest were disbelievers deserving punishment.
STUDYQURAN:11:116/r1.anchor: The Shiite Quran commentator al-Ṭūsī observes that, in asking the question in v. 116, God intends to produce wonder and amazement

STUDYQURAN:11:116/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:11:116/r2.speaker: al-Ṭūsī
STUDYQURAN:11:116/r2.claim: Al-Ṭūsī's reading highlights that only a few in earlier communities were righteous, while most were disbelievers who merited punishment.
STUDYQURAN:11:116/r2.anchor: that in past communities there were only a few who were righteous while the rest were disbelievers who deserved punishment.

TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī asks why past generations whose stories were recounted were not equipped with people of insight who could reflect on God's admonitions and proofs and understand the stakes of belief and unbelief.
TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r1.anchor: بمعصيتهم إياي وكفرهم برسلي من قبلكم

TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r2.claim: “People of baqiyya” means people endowed with understanding and reason who consider God's admonitions and proofs.

TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r3.claim: They warn sinners against disobedience and those who disbelieve in God against disbelief on His earth.
TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r3.anchor: ينهون أهل المعاصي عن معاصيهم وأهل الكفر بالله عن كفرهم به في أرضه

TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r4.claim: Only a few forbade corruption; God saved them when He punished those who persisted in disbelief, and they were the followers of the prophets and messengers.
TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r4.anchor: إلا يسيرا، فإنهم كانوا ينهون عن الفساد في الأرض، فنجاهم الله من عذابه، حين أخذ

TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r5.claim: Qalīlan is accusative because it is a disconnected exception, as in the exception of Jonah's people; al-Ṭabarī says he has explained this elsewhere.
TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r5.anchor: ونصب «قليلا» لأن قوله: {إلا قليلا} [البقرة: 83] استثناء منقطع مما قبله، كما قال: {إلا قوم يونس لما آمنوا} [يونس: 98]

TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says the few are those who were saved when God's punishment descended.
TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد: " اعتذر فقال: {فلولا كان من القرون من قبلكم} [هود: 116] حتى بلغ: {إلا قليلا ممن أنجينا منهم} [هود: 116] فإذا هم الذين نجوا حين نزل عذاب الله.

TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj says God counts them as few from each nation.
TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r7.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قوله: " {فلولا كان من القرون من قبلكم أولو بقية} إلى قوله: {إلا قليلا ممن أنجينا منهم} [هود: 116] قال: يستقلهم الله من كل قوم

TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r8.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains that God saved Noah, Hūd, Ṣāliḥ, and their believers while destroying the peoples who had enjoyed worldly ease; when Bilāl asked him about his explanation, he considered al-Ḥasan's account a sound answer.
TAB-FULL:v12p627#2/r8.anchor: سمعت الحسن يقول: " {قيل يا نوح اهبط بسلام منا وبركات عليك وعلى أمم ممن معك

TAB-FULL:v12p629/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p629/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v12p629/r1.claim: Qatāda says that before this community, only a few people forbade corruption, and God saved them.
TAB-FULL:v12p629/r1.anchor: عن قتادة " {فلولا كان من القرون من قبلكم أولو بقية ينهون عن الفساد في الأرض إلا قليلا

TAB-FULL:v12p629/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p629/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p629/r2.claim: Those who wronged themselves followed the worldly ease and pleasures they had been given, preferring them to the afterlife's deeds and what would save them from God's punishment.
TAB-FULL:v12p629/r2.anchor: وقوله: {واتبع الذين ظلموا ما أترفوا فيه} [هود: 116] يقول تعالى ذكره: واتبع الذين ظلموا أنفسهم، فكفروا بالله ما أترفوا فيه

TAB-FULL:v12p629/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p629/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v12p629/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses what they enjoyed as what they were given respite to pursue.
TAB-FULL:v12p629/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: " {واتبع الذين ظلموا ما أترفوا فيه} [هود: 116] قال: ما أنظروا فيه "

TAB-FULL:v12p629/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p629/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v12p629/r4.claim: Qatāda interprets it as their worldly life.
TAB-FULL:v12p629/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {واتبع الذين ظلموا ما أترفوا فيه} [هود: 116] من دنياهم

TAB-FULL:v12p629/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p629/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v12p629/r5.claim: Mujāhid says they followed their kingship and tyranny and abandoned the truth.
TAB-FULL:v12p629/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله: " {واتبع الذين ظلموا ما أترفوا فيه} [هود: 116] قال: في ملكهم وتجبرهم، وتركوا الحق "

TAB-FULL:v12p629/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p629/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p629/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī's synthesis is that they pursued worldly pleasures, became arrogant and disbelieved, rebelled against God's command, and blocked His path; in Arabic, a mutraf is someone raised in luxury and fed pleasures.
TAB-FULL:v12p629/r6.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب أن يقال: إن الله تعالى ذكره أخبر أن الذين ظلموا أنفسهم من كل أمة سلفت

TAB-FULL:v12p629/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p629/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p629/r7.claim: In Arabic, a mutraf is someone indulged in luxury and nourished by pleasures.
TAB-FULL:v12p629/r7.anchor: وذلك أن المترف في كلام العرب: هو المنعم الذي قد غذي باللذات، ومنه قول الراجز: [البحر الرجز]

TAB-FULL:v12p630/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p630/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p630/r1.claim: He cites the line about guiding the heads of wealthy oppressors to the Commander of the Faithful as poetic evidence in this discussion.
TAB-FULL:v12p630/r1.anchor: تهدي رءوس المترفين الصداد … إلى أمير المؤمنين الممتاد

TAB-FULL:v12p630/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p630/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p630/r2.claim: The wrongdoers were people who acquired disbelief in God.

TABATABAI:11:116-119/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:116-119/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:116-119/r1.claim: The people remaining after the exception are the majority; they are unjust, pursued the worldly luxuries in which they lived, and were criminals.
TABATABAI:11:116-119/r1.anchor: بيان حال الباقي منهم بعد الاستثناء وهم أكثرهم وعرفهم بأنهم الذين ظلموا وبين أنهم اتبعوا لذائذ الدنيا التي اترفوا فيها وكانوا مجرمين

TABATABAI:11:116-119/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:116-119/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:116-119/r2.claim: The exception and description divide people into two classes: those God saves and the criminals; the following verse develops this division through differing and mercy.
TABATABAI:11:116-119/r2.anchor: وقد تحصل بهذا الاستثناء وهذا الباقي الذي ذكر حالهم تقسيم الناس إلى صنفين مختلفين الناجون بإنجاء الله والمجرمون ولذلك عقبه

TABRISI:11:116/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:11:116/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:11:116/r6.claim: The verse follows the account of destroyed nations: they brought ruin on themselves; God would have spared them if believers had enjoined reform and forbidden corruption, but widespread disbelief merited total destruction.
TABRISI:11:116/r6.anchor: وجه اتصال قوله تعالى { فلولا كان من القرون من قبلكم } الآية

FARRA:v2p30/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p30/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p30/r2.claim: Almost no earlier people did this; a small group forbade corruption and were saved. The exception is disconnected, like Jonah’s people in 10:98; nominative is also valid.
FARRA:v2p30/r2.anchor: يقول لم يكن منهم أحد كذلك إلا قليلا أي هؤلاء كانوا ينهون فنجوا.

FARRA:v2p30/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p30/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p30/r3.claim: One explanation is that wrongdoers followed familiar worldly luxury and preferred pleasures to the afterlife.
FARRA:v2p30/r3.anchor: اتبعوا في دنياهم ما عودوا من النعيم وإيثار اللذات على أمر الآخرة.

FARRA:v2p30/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p30/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p30/r4.claim: Another explanation is that they followed their sins and evil deeds to the Fire.
FARRA:v2p30/r4.anchor: ويقال: اتبعوا ذنوبهم وأعمالهم السيئة إلى النار.

THALABI:v5p194/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p194/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p194/r1.claim: Falawlā means fa-halā: why were there no people of religion and reason in earlier destroyed generations to forbid corruption?
THALABI:v5p194/r1.anchor: فلولا كان فهلا كان من القرون التي أهلكناهم من قبلكم أولوا بقية أصحاب دين وعقل

THALABI:v5p194/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p194/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p194/r2.claim: The interrogative carries a sense of negation, so the phrase means that such people did not exist.
THALABI:v5p194/r2.anchor: ومعناه: فلم يكن، لأن في الاستفهام ضربا من الجحد

THALABI:v5p194/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p194/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p194/r3.claim: The exception is disconnected; those saved were followers of the prophets and people of truth.
THALABI:v5p194/r3.anchor: إلا قليلا استثناء منقطع ممن أنجينا منهم وهم أتباع الأنبياء وأهل الحق

THALABI:v5p194/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p194/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v5p194/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses their luxuries as what they were allowed or given to enjoy.
THALABI:v5p194/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ما أنظروا فيه

THALABI:v5p194/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p194/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v5p194/r5.claim: A second gloss attributed to Ibn Abbas says they were made insolent by their comforts.

THALABI:v5p194/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p194/r6.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v5p194/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses the phrase as making excuses.

THALABI:v5p194/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p194/r7.speaker: مقاتل بن سليمان
THALABI:v5p194/r7.claim: Muqatil ibn Sulayman glosses it as what they were given.

THALABI:v5p194/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p194/r8.speaker: ابن حيان
THALABI:v5p194/r8.claim: Ibn Hayyan glosses it as what they were bestowed or entrusted with.

THALABI:v5p194/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p194/r9.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v5p194/r9.claim: Mujahid says they became tyrannical in rule and defied God's command.
THALABI:v5p194/r9.anchor: مجاهد: تجبروا في الملك وعتوا عن أمر الله

THALABI:v5p194/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p194/r10.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v5p194/r10.claim: Al-Farraʾ reads it as the luxuries and pleasures they chose, preferring worldly life to the afterlife.
THALABI:v5p194/r10.anchor: الفراء: ما سودوا من النعيم واللذات وإيثار الدنيا على الآخرة

THALABI:v5p194/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p194/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p194/r11.claim: He identifies the criminals here as disbelievers.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p584/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p584/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p584/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Farrāʾ take lawlā as negation: no people among the earlier destroyed nations were like this, as in 10:98.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p584/r1.anchor: ومعنى (لولا) هاهنا نفي عند المفسرين، وهو قول ابن عباس (¬2): يريد ما كان من القرون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p584/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p584/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p584/r2.claim: Another view takes lawlā in its ordinary sense, “why were there not?”—a reproach to disbelievers for following earlier peoples into corruption.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p584/r2.anchor: ومن الناس (¬4) من يقول: (لولا) هاهنا على ظاهره، بمعنى (هلا كان)، و (لم لا كان)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p584/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p584/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p584/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses ūlū baqiyya as people possessing religion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p584/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬6): يريد: أولو دين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p584/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p584/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p584/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj glosses the phrase as possessing discernment, or obedience; baqiyya in a person means praiseworthy excellence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p584/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج (¬7): {أولو بقية}] (¬8) معناه أولو تمييز، ويجوز أولو طاعة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p584/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p584/r5.speaker: القتبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p584/r5.claim: Al-Qutaybī explains it as having a remnant of religion; people “with a remnant” have firmness and goodness.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p210#6/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p210#6/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p210#6/r1.claim: Falawlā here means “why did there not” or “if only.”
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p210#6/r1.anchor: فلولا كان من القرون من قبلكم} أي: فهلا.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p210#6/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p210#6/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p210#6/r2.claim: People of baqiyya are people with a remnant of religion, moral firmness, and goodness.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p210#6/r2.anchor: أولو بقية} أي: أولو بقية من دين. يقال: [قوم] لهم بقية وفيهم بقية.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p210#6/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p210#6/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p210#6/r3.claim: The wrongdoers followed the wealth they had been given, preferring it and being tempted by it.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p210#6/r3.anchor: واتبع الذين ظلموا ما أترفوا فيه} ما أعطوا من الأموال؛ أي: آثروه واتبعوه ففتنوا به (1) .

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p585/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p585/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p585/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses corruption as associating partners with God, violating God's rights, and disobedience.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p585/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد عن الشرك والاعتداء في حقوق الله والمعصية.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p585/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p585/r2.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p585/r2.claim: Al-Farra and al-Zajjaj treat the exception as disconnected: it means rather, a few whom God saved did forbid corruption, as with Jonah's people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p585/r2.anchor: قال الفراء (¬3) والزجاج (¬4): هو استثناء على الانقطاع مما قبله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p585/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p585/r3.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p585/r3.claim: The few saved people who forbade corruption were the prophets' followers and people of truth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p585/r3.anchor: قال المفسرون (¬5): وهم أتباع الأنبياء وأهل الحق.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p585/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p585/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p585/r4.claim: Tarfah means blessing; a pampered child is comfortable in body, and a mutraf is spoiled by luxury and abundant living.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p585/r4.anchor: الترفة النعمة وصبي مترف (¬6) إذا كان منعم البدن، والمترف الذي أبطرته النعمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p585/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p585/r5.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p585/r5.claim: Al-Farra says they followed their accustomed worldly luxury, preferred pleasures to the afterlife, and relied on worldly wealth and goods.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p585/r5.anchor: قال الفراء (¬8): يقول اتبعوا في دنياهم ما عودوا من النعيم وإيثار اللذات على أمر الآخرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p585/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p585/r6.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p585/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas, as transmitted by Ata, explains that they followed what God had expanded and bestowed on them; another report says they luxuriated and became insolent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p585/r6.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس (¬1) يريد: اتبعوا (¬2) ما وسعت عليهم وأنعمت، وروي (¬3) عنه نعموا وأبطروا أيضا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p289/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p289/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p289/r1.claim: Without a following answer, لولا can mean هلا, as in the rebuke about earlier peoples and the poet's question why they do not count the armed hero.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p289/r1.anchor: لولا تكون في بعض الأحوال بمعنى: هلا وذلك إذا رأيتها بغير جواب،

ELMALILI:11:116/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:116/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:116/r1.claim: The phrase describes virtuous communities among earlier Mosaic and Christian adherents: pious people who serve what endures and benefit others.
ELMALILI:11:116/r1.anchor: Mûsevî Îsevî gibi eski dinlere mensup olanlardan bekāya hizmet eder

ELMALILI:11:116/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:116/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:116/r2.claim: Earlier nations had almost no such virtuous community to restrain corruption; only a small number whom God saved remained.
ELMALILI:11:116/r2.anchor: Lâkin içlerinden necat verdiğimiz pek az kimselerden başka yok

ELMALILI:11:116/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:116/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:116/r3.claim: The wrongdoers include those who actively committed corruption and those who neglected to forbid it, thereby wronging themselves and causing their destruction.
ELMALILI:11:116/r3.anchor: bilfiil fesad yaparak veya nehyi terk ederek kendilerine zulmetmiş, helâklerine sebep olmuş olanlar

ELMALILI:11:116/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:116/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:116/r4.claim: They pursued the pleasures of the luxurious life in which they had been indulged.

ELMALILI:11:116/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:11:116/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:11:116/r5.claim: The destruction of earlier peoples had two causes: no more than a small minority restrained corruption, while the affluent pursued pleasure and led people astray.
ELMALILI:11:116/r5.anchor: İşte mukaddemâ helâk olan akvâmın helâklerine sebep bu ikisidir

MAJAZ:v1p301/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p301/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p301/r1.claim: What the wrongdoers indulged in means their arrogance against God’s command, turning away from it, and disbelief; the cited poem calls the affluent ‘the arrogant.’
MAJAZ:v1p301/r1.anchor: ما أترفوا فيه» (117) أي ما تجبروا وتكبروا عن أمر الله وصدوا عنه وكفروا، قال: تهدى رؤوس المترفين الصداد

MAJAZ:v1p301/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p301/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p301/r2.claim: Al-mumtād in the cited verse derives from māda yamīdu.
MAJAZ:v1p301/r2.anchor: إلى أمير المؤمنين الممتاد الممتاد من ماد يميد.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:116/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:116/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:116/r1.claim: These verses summarize the sura's account of why earlier peoples were destroyed and stress the need for virtuous people to oppose social evil.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:116/r1.anchor: Bu âyetlerde sûrenin bir özeti yapılmakta, sûrede helâk olduğu bildirilen kavimlerin helâk oluş sebepleri genel olarak ifade edilmekte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:116/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:116/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:116/r2.claim: Few people of virtue and sound judgment arose among earlier generations to prevent corruption on earth.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:116/r2.anchor: 116. âyet Hz. Peygamber’den önceki nesiller içerisinde yeryüzünde kötülükleri önleyecek erdemli ve birikimli kimselerin az olduğunu haber vermektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:116/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:116/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:116/r3.claim: In corrupt societies, most people set aside moral concerns, pursued pleasures in prosperity's heedlessness, and became immersed in sin.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:116/r3.anchor: Kötülüğün yaygınlaştığı toplumlarda ahlâkî endişelere yer vermeyen çoğunluk, refahın getirdiği şımarıklıkla zevklerinin peşine düşerek günaha gömülmüşlerdi.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:116/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:116/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:116/r4.claim: The peoples' destruction was the consequence of their own conduct, not God's injustice; God does not destroy those who abandon evil and reform.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:116/r4.anchor: Onların bu duruma düşmeleri Allah’ın zulmü değil kendi davranışlarının bir sonucudur. Çünkü Allah kötülüklerden vazgeçip durumlarını düzeltmeye çalışanları helâk etmez.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:116/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:116/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:116/r5.claim: They rejected prophets sent to reform their beliefs and circumstances, squandered their opportunity, and accumulated injustice until divine punishment became due.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:116/r5.anchor: Onlar inançlarını ıslah etmek, durumlarını düzeltmek maksadıyla gönderilen peygamberleri tanımadılar, kendilerine verilen fırsatı değerlendirmediler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:116/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:116/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:116/r6.claim: A society will not be destroyed while people remain who commend good, prevent evil, and establish right and justice; without them, its destruction is inevitable.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:11:116/r6.anchor: Bir toplumda iyiliği tavsiye edip kötülüğü önleyecek, hak ve adaleti tesis edecek kimseler bulunduğu sürece o toplum yok olmaz

BURHAN:v4p377/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p377/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p377/r1.claim: Lawla used for reproach or regret normally precedes a past verb; exhortation and reproach concern actions, so it takes a verb.

BURHAN:v4p377/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p377/r7.speaker: ابن فارس والهروي
BURHAN:v4p377/r7.claim: Ibn Faris and al-Harawi report a fourth use of lawla for negation, meaning lam, in the examples about a believing town and earlier generations.
BURHAN:v4p377/r7.anchor: ذكره ابن فارس في كتاب فقه العربية والهروي في الأزهية

BURHAN:v4p377/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p377/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p377/r8.claim: The author prefers the apparent exhortative sense, supported by Ubayy's reading fahlā; reproach with a past verb nevertheless implies that the action did not occur.
BURHAN:v4p377/r8.anchor: والظاهر إن المراد فهلا ويؤيده أنها في مصحف أبي

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p202/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p202/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p202/r1.claim: Baqiyyah derives from baqāʾ; al-bāqī persists through successive times, while baqiyyah is what remains when its company disappears at once.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p202/r1.anchor: البقية مشتقة من البقاء . والباقي : ما تكررت عليه الأزمان وهو باق .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p202/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p202/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p202/r2.claim: Some Arabs use baqā in place of baqiya; yubqī can mean to watch or keep something under observation.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p202/r2.anchor: ومن العرب من يقول : بقى مكان بقي . يقال : فلان يبقي الشيء إذا رقبه ورصده .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p202/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p202/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p202/r3.claim: A hadith uses abqaynā rasūl Allāh to mean that the Companions waited for the Messenger.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p202/r3.anchor: وفي الحديث : ( وأبقينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ) . يعني انتظرناه .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p202/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p202/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p202/r4.claim: Baqiyyah here means a small number of people who would forbid corruption.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p202/r4.anchor: أحدها : القليل ، ومنه قوله تعالى في هود

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p532/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p532/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p532/r1.claim: Lولا originally prevents one thing because another exists: were it not for disobedience, one would have been treated well.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p532/r1.anchor: ' لولا ' ( في الأصل ) : حرف وضع لامتناع الشيء لوجود غيره

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p532/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p532/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p532/r3.claim: A second use means ‘there was not’; some scholars treat it as a form of the preceding halā sense.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p532/r3.anchor: والثاني : بمعنى لم يكن . ومنه قوله تعالى في يونس

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p532/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p532/r6.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p532/r6.claim: Ibn Qutayba says lولا without a response means halā, but when it has a response it does not carry that meaning.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p532/r6.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة إذا رأيت ' لولا ' بلا جواب فهي بمعنى : هلا

BURHAN:v4p239/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p239/r4.speaker: المبرد والجرمي
BURHAN:v4p239/r4.claim: Al-Mubarrad and al-Jarmi say a nominative reading قليل would be sound as an adjective after a disconnected exception.
BURHAN:v4p239/r4.anchor: قال المبرد والجرمي في قوله تعالى

BURHAN:v4p375/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p375/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p375/r9.claim: A second use of لولا is exhortation or urging, and in this use it takes an imperfect verb.

DAMGHANI:v1p75/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p75/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p75/r8.claim: Baqiyyah can mean a small number of people.
DAMGHANI:v1p75/r8.anchor: البقية يعني القلة . قوله تعالى في سورة هود
